Luka Dončić (; born February 28, 1999) is a Slovenian professional basketball player for the Los Angeles Lakers of the National Basketball Association (NBA). He has also played for the Dallas Mavericks. He also plays for the Slovenia national team. On February 2, 2025, the Mavericks traded Dončić along with Maxi Kleber and Markieff Morris to the Los Angeles Lakers in exchange for Max Christie, Anthony Davis and a 2029 first-round pick. Jalen Hood-Schifino and a 2025 second-round pick were also traded to the Utah Jazz. The Jazz also received a 2025 second-round pick from the Mavericks. Dončić did not expect the trade and it is considered to be one of the most unexpected trades in NBA history. Dončić can speak four languages: Slovenian, Serbian, English, and Spanish. He learned Spanish after joining Real Madrid.

Lukas Josef Gugganig (born February 14, 1995 in Spittal an der Drau) is an Austrian football player. He plays defender for SCR Altach in the Austrian Bundesliga Gugganig started in 2002 in the youth ranks of SC Mühldorf in Carinthia. From there he moved to the FC Red Bull Salzburg academy in 2009. 2012/13 season he was transferred to FC Liefering. He made his debut in the Austrian Bundesliga on April 12, 2015 in the 3-3 away match against SK Rapid Wien. For the 2015/16 season he moved to the German second division club FSV Frankfurt. After relegation with Frankfurt in 2016, he moved to SpVgg Greuther Fürth. For the 2019/20 seasonhe went to VfL Osnabrück. Gugganig returned to Austria for the 2022/23 season and moved to Bundesliga club SCR Altach. Gugganig played international matches for the Austrian youth national teams from U16 to U19. With the U19 national team he qualified for the 2014 European Championships in Hungary. His strong performances led to him being called up to the Austrian U21 team.

Luka Lipošinović (Serbian Cyrillic: Лука Липошиновић; 12 May 1933 – 26 September 1992) was a Yugoslav footballer and manager. He played for Yugoslavia at the 1956 Summer Olympics and at the 1958 FIFA World Cup. Silver medalist at the 1956 Summer Olympics

Lukas Reichel (born 17 May 2002) is a German professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Providence Bruins of the American Hockey League (AHL). He has also played for the Chicago Blackhawks and Vancouver Canucks. Outside of the NHL, Reichel played for the Eisbären Berlin of the Deutsche Eishockey Liga (DEL). Before playing in the NHL, Reichel played four years with the Eisbären Berlin of the Western Collegiate Hockey Association (WCHA). He had a successful time with the Mavericks. He was named to the WCHA All-Tournament Team and the All-WCHA First Teams. He helped the Eisbären during the playoffs. They defeated the Iserlohn Roosters and ERC Ingolstadt. They went on to defeat Grizzlys Wolfsburg two games to one in the Final to win the DEL Championship. He was drafted 17th overall by the Chicago Blackhawks in the 2020 NHL entry draft. On 9 June 2021, Reichel signed a two-year, $1.85 million entry-level contract to join the Blackhawks. They sent him down to play for their AHL-affiliate Rockford IceHogs. On 13 January 2022, the Blackhawks called him up and Reichel made his NHL debut in a 3–2 overtime win against the Montreal Canadiens. On 16 April, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Dominik Kubalík goal in a 4–3 loss against the Nashville Predators. On 8 January 2023, Reichel scored his first NHL goal against Jacob Markström in a 4–3 overtime win against the Calgary Flames. He also assisted on goals from Philipp Kurashev and Max Domi to cap off a three point game. On 7 May 2024, Reichel signed a two-year, $2.4 million contract to stay with the Blackhawks. On 24 October 2025, the Blackhawks traded Reichel to the Vancouver Canucks in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round draft pick. After 14 regular season games, the Canucks waived him and sent him down to play for their AHL-affiliate Abbotsford Canucks. On 6 March 2026, the Canucks traded Reichel to the Boston Bruins in exchange for a 2026 sixth-round draft pick. Reichel's father Martin Reichel, uncle Robert Reichel, and cousin Kristian Reichel were also hockey players. Martin played for Germany at the 2002 Winter Olympics, Robert played 11 seasons in the NHL, and Kristian 15 games in the NHL.

Luke Evangelista (born February 21, 2002) is a Canadian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Nashville Predators of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Evangelista played three seasons with the London Knights of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with the Knights. He was named to the Second All-Star Team. He was drafted 42nd overall by the Nashville Predators in the 2020 NHL entry draft. On November 9, 2020, Evangelista signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Sharks. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Milwaukee Admirals. On October 2, 2019, the Predators called him up and Evangelista made his NHL debut in a 3–1 loss against the Pittsburgh Penguins. Two days later on October 4, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Matt Duchene goal in a 2–1 loss against the Florida Panthers. On December 28, Evangelista scored his first two NHL goals back-to-back against Artūrs Šilovs in a 4–3 shootout loss against the Vancouver Canucks. On August 4, 2022, Evangelista signed a four-year, $3.25 million contract to stay with the Sharks. On October 3, 2025, Evangelista signed a two-year, $6 million contract to stay with the Predators. Evangelista's second cousin is supermodel Linda Evangelista and he is also second cousin's with former NHLer and Hockey Hall of Famer Brendan Shanahan.

Luke Glendening (born April 28, 1989) is an American professional ice hockey forward. He is currently an unrestricted free agent. He has played for the Detroit Red Wings, Dallas Stars, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils, and Philadelphia Flyers in the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Glendening played four years with the Michigan Wolverines of the Central Collegiate Hockey Association (CCHA). He was not drafted by an NHL team. On June 19, 2012, Glendening signed a one-year contract to join the Grand Rapids Griffins of the American Hockey League (AHL). He also played for the Toledo Walleye of the ECHL. He won the Calder Cup with the Griffins in 2012. On June 19, 2012, Glendening signed a one-year, $575,000 entry-level contract to join the Detroit Red Wings of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was sent back down to play for their AHL-affiliate Grand Rapids Griffins. On October 12, 2013, the Wings called him up and Glendening made his NHL debut in a 5–2 win against the Philadelphia Flyers. On December 17, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Daniel Cleary goal in a 5–2 loss against the Anaheim Ducks. On April 5, 2014, Glendening scored his first NHL goal against Carey Price in a 5–3 loss against the Montreal Canadiens. On July 14, 2016, Glendening signed a four-year, $7.2 million contract to stay with the Wings. On July 28, 2021, Glendening signed a two-year, $3 million contract to join the Dallas Stars. He scored 12 goals and recorded 10 assists in his two regular seasons, as well as scoring 2 goals and recording as assist in playoff series with the Stars. On July 1, 2023, Glendening signed a two-year, $1.6 million contract to join the Tampa Bay Lightning. He scored 14 goals and recorded 4 assists in his two regular seasons, as well as scoring a goals and recording as assist in playoff series with the Lightning. On October 7, 2025, Glendening signed a one-year contract to join the New Jersey Devils. He recorded four assists in 52 regular season games with the Devils. On March 6, 2026, the Devils placed Glendening onto waivers and his contract was picked up by the Philadelphia Flyers. He scored two goals and recorded three assists in 18 regular season games, as well as, one goal in 10 playoff games with the Flyers.

Luke McCormick (born 15 August 1983) is a former English football player. He was born in Coventry, England. He is a goalkeeper. He plays for the English football team Swindon Town. In the 2003–04 season, McCormick played when Romain Larrieu could not. Larrieu injured his knee. McCormick played instead. Plymouth Argyle beat Stockport County on 24 January 2004. The score was 2-0. In this match McCormick set a new club record of seven clean sheets in a row. A clean sheet is a game where the other side gets no goals. McCormick was voted the most promising player of the 2003–04 season by Plymouth Argyle fans. On 7 June 2008. McCormick was arrested on suspicion for killing two people by dangerous driving. Subsequently, he was released by Plymouth Arygle and was jailed for seven years on 6 October 2008. He was let out of prison in June 2012.

Luke Littler (born 21 January 2007) is an English professional darts player from Warrington who plays in Professional Darts Corporation events. He is the current PDC World Youth Champion, the current Bahrain Masters Champion, and the current Belgian Darts Open champion. Littler is the youngest player to have won a match in the WDF World Darts Championship, and PDC World Darts Championship. He is the youngest player to reach the PDC World Darts Championship final, aged 16 years, and both the youngest ever player to hit a televised nine-dart finish and the youngest to hit 2 televised nine darters. The first one he achieved, at the 2024 Bahrain Darts Masters aged 16, and the second, he achieved at the 2024 Belgian Darts Open aged 17. As well as this, Littler is the youngest ever player to hit a broadcast nine-darter. He achieved this at the age of 14 in 2021. He earned more than £350,000 in prize money in the first three months of 2024. He has more than 1.2 million followers on Instagram and 178,000 on X.

Luke Schenn (born November 2, 1989) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Winnipeg Jets of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the New York Rangers. Schenn is a two-time Stanley Cup champion, winning back-to-back with the Lightning in 2020 and 2021. Before playing in the NHL, Schenn played three seasons with the Kelowna Rockets of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He had a successful time with his teams. He was named the Kelowna Rockets Rookie of the Year after finishing his rookie season scoring 3 goals and recording 8 assists for 11 points. He was also named a West Second Team All-Star. He was drafted 5th overall by the Toronto Maple Leafs in the 2008 NHL entry draft. On October 7, 2008, Schenn signed a three-year, $1.25 million entry-level contract to join the Leafs. On February 9, 2018, Schenn made his NHL debut in a 3–2 win against the Detroit Red Wings. On February 13, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Matt Stajan goal in a 6–5 shootout win against the New Jersey Devils. On February 7, 2009, Schenn scored his first NHL goal against Carey Price in a 5–2 win against the Montreal Canadiens. On September 16, 2011, Schenn signed a five-year, $18 million contract to stay with the Leafs. On June 23, 2012, the Leafs traded Schenn to the Philadelphia Flyers in exchange for James van Riemsdyk. With the trade, Luke was able to play alongside his younger brother Brayden who was also playing for the Flyers at the time. Schenn played four seasons with the Flyers. On January 6, 2016, the Flyers traded Schenn along with Vincent Lecavalier to the Los Angeles Kings in exchange for Jordan Weal and a 2016 third-round draft pick. He scored 2 goals and recorded 9 assists for 11 points in 43 regular season games. On July 23, 2016, Schenn signed a two-year, $2.5 million contract to join the Arizona Coyotes. He played two seasons with the Coyotes. On July 2, 2018, Schenn signed a one-year, $800,000 contract to join the Anaheim Ducks. He played 8 regular season games before being sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate San Diego Gulls. On January 16, 2019, the Ducks traded Schenn along with a 2020 seventh-round draft pick to the Vancouver Canucks in exchange for Michael Del Zotto. He played 18 regular season games with the Canucks and recorded 2 assists. On July 1, 2019, Schenn signed a one-year, $700,000 contract to join the Tampa Bay Lightning. He was a healthy scratch and was with the team when they won the Stanley Cup that year. On October 9, 2020, Schenn signed a one-year, $800,000 contract to stay with the Lightning. He was with the team when they won another Stanley Cup that year as well. On July 28, 2021, Schenn signed a two-year, $1.7 million contract to return to the Vancouver Canucks. He played two seasons in his return to the Canucks. On March 1, 2023, the Canucks traded Schenn back to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for a 2023 third-round draft pick. In his return to the Leafs, he scored 1 goal in 15 regular season games and recorded 1 assist in 11 playoff games. On July 1, 2023, Schenn signed a three-year, $8.25 million contract to join the Nashville Predators. On October 17, 2024, Schenn played in his 1,000 career NHL game in a 4–2 loss against the Edmonton Oilers. On March 5, 2025, the Predators traded Schenn along with Tommy Novak to the Pittsburgh Penguins in exchange for Michael Bunting and a 2026 fourth-round draft pick. He never played a game for the Penguins. Two days later on March 7, the Penguins traded Schenn to the Winnipeg Jets in exchange for a 2026 second-round draft pick and a 2027 fourth-round draft pick. He played parts of two seasons with the Jets. On March 5, 2026, the Jets traded Schenn along with Logan Stanley to the Buffalo Sabres in exchange for Jacob Bryson, Isak Rosen, a 2026 conditional fourth-round draft pick, and a 2027 second-round draft pick. Schenn's younger brother Brayden is also a professional hockey player for the New York Islanders.

Luke Warren Hughes (born September 9, 2003) is an American professional ice hockey center. He currently plays for the New Jersey Devils of the National Hockey League (NHL). Hughes was the co-cover athlete for EA Sports' NHL 25 along with his brothers Jack and Quinn. Before playing in the NHL, Hughes played nine playoff games for U.S. National Development Team of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and two years for the Michigan Wolverines of the Big Ten Conference (B1G). He had a successful time with his teams. He was named the Big Ten Co-Freshman of the Year and was named to the All-Big Ten Freshman Team, All-Big Ten First Team, All-Big Ten Second Team, and Big Ten All-Tournament Team. He was also named both a AHCA West First and Second Team All-American. He was drafted 4th overall by the New Jersey Devils of the 2021 NHL entry draft. On April 8, 2023, Hughes signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Devils. On April 11, 2023, Hughes made his NHL debut in a 6–2 win against the Buffalo Sabres. On October 17, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Erik Haula goal in a 5–4 overtime win against the Washington Capitals. Later in the game, Hughes scored his first NHL goal against Darcy Kuemper which was also the overtime winning goal. On October 1, 2025, Hughes signed an seven-year, $63 million contract to stay with the Devils. Hughes is Jewish. Hughes comes from a hockey family. His brothers Quinn and Jack are also professional hockey players.

Luke Kunin (born December 4, 1997) is an American professional ice hockey center. He is currently an unrestricted free agent. He has played for the Minnesota Wild, Nashville Predators, San Jose Sharks, Columbus Blue Jackets, and Florida Panthers of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Kunin played two seasons with the U.S. National Development Team of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and two years with the Wisconsin Badgers of the Big Ten Conference (B1G). He was named to the All-Big Ten Freshman Team, All-Big Ten Second Team, Big Ten All-Tournament Team, and was also named a AHCA West Second-Team All-American. He was drafted 15th overall by the Minnesota Wild of the 2016 NHL entry draft. On March 23, 2017, Kunin signed a three-year, $4.275 million entry-level contract to join the Wild. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Iowa Wild. On October 14, 2017, Minnesota called him up and Kunin made his NHL debut in a 5–4 overtime loss against the Columbus Blue Jackets. On October 21, he recorded his first two NHL point after assisting on goals from Ryan Suter and Daniel Winnik in a 4–2 win against the Calgary Flames. On October 26, Kunin scored his first NHL goal short-handed against Thomas Greiss in a 6–4 win against the New York Islanders. On October 7, 2020, the Wild traded Kunin along with a 2020 third-round draft pick to the Nashville Predators in exchange for Nick Bonino, a 2020 second-round draft pick, and a 2020 fourth-round draft pick. On January 6, 2021, Kunin signed a two-year, $4.6 million contract to stay with the Predators. On July 8, 2022, the Predators traded Kunin to the San Jose Sharks in exchange for John Leonard and a 2023 third-round draft pick. On July 18, 2022, Kunin signed a two-year, $5.5 million contract to stay with the Sharks. On June 30, 2024, Kunin signed a one-year, $2.75 million contract to stay with the Sharks. On March 7, 2025, the Sharks traded Kunin to the Columbus Blue Jackets in exchange for a 2025 fourth-round draft pick. He played 12 regular season games for the Jackets. On August 22, 2025, Kunin signed a one-year, $775,000 contract to join the Florida Panthers. Kunin is Jewish and lives with type 1 diabetes. He is married to former professional hockey player Sophia Kunin.

Lulu Zaharani Krisna Widodo (born December 16, 2003) is an Indonesian model, athlete, and beauty pageant titleholder who was crowned Puteri Indonesia Pariwisata 2023. Lulu Zahrani will represent Indonesia at the Miss Charm 2024 event which will take place in Vietnam.

Luna Fokke (born 9 March 2001) is a Dutch women's field hockey player who currently plays as a midfielder for HC Kampong. As a member of the Netherland national team (under-21) she became 2022 Junior World Cup champion. Fokke is Born in 2001 and lived in Leidschendam. At the age of six years old she started playing field hockey at and later moved to HGC in Wassenaar. In the last match she played with HGC she made the only goal in the match, which resulted in the team being promoted to the main league. At the time she has finished high school and moved to Utrecht. She started studying computer science and started playing field hockey with HC Kampong in 2019. Playing as a midfielder, she scores very often. As a member of the national team (under-18) she became 2018 Girls' EuroHockey Youth Championships champion. She was a member of the Netherland national team (under-21) that became world champion at the 2022 Women's FIH Hockey Junior World Cup in South Africa. She scored at these championships a total of 11 goals.

Luol Deng (born 16 April 1985) is a former South Sudanese-born British professional basketball player. He played in the National Basketball Association (NBA) for the Chicago Bulls (2004–2014), the Cleveland Cavaliers (2014), the Miami Heat (2014–2016), the Los Angeles Lakers (2016–2018) and the Minnesota Timberwolves (2018–2019). He became a British citizen in 2006, and played for the Great Britain national team. He played college basketball for the Duke Blue Devils. Deng was born in Wau, Sudan (now South Sudan). His father is politician Aldo Deng. His older brother, Ajou Deng, was also a basketball player.
Luo Yiwei (born 18 January 1990) is a Singapoean track cyclist. She competed at the 2017 South-East Asian Games, 2018 Commonwealth Games, and 2021 UCI Track Cycling Championships.

Lusia Harris-Stewart (born Lusia Harris; February 10, 1955 – January 18, 2022) was an American basketball player. She played for Delta State University. She won three Association for Intercollegiate Athletics for Women (AIAW) National Championships. She represented the United States' national team and won the silver medal in the 1976 Olympic Games. She played professional basketball with the Houston Angels of the Women's Professional Basketball League (WBL). She was the first and only woman ever officially drafted by the National Basketball Association (NBA). Harris was honored into to the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame and Women's Basketball Hall of Fame. Harris died on January 18, 2022 in Greenwood, Mississippi at the age of 66.

Robert Luther "Lute" Olson (September 22, 1934 – August 27, 2020) was an American Hall of Fame basketball coach. He was born in Mayville, North Dakota. He was also honored in the National Collegiate Basketball Hall of Fame (2006) and re-inducted in the class of 2019. He was the head coach of the University of Arizona's men's team for 25 years. He was also head coach at the University of Iowa for nine years and California State University, Long Beach for one season. On October 23, 2008, Olson announced his retirement from coaching. Olson died on August 27, 2020 under hospice care in Tucson, Arizona from stroke-related problems at the age of 85.

Luton Shelton (11 November 1985 – 22 January 2021) was a Jamaican footballer. He played as a striker or winger. He made his international debut for Jamaica in 2004. In 2018, it was announced that Shelton has been diagnosed with ALS. He died from problems caused by the disease on 22 January 2021, aged 35.

Luís Filipe Madeira Caeiro Figo OIH (born 4 November 1972) is a former Portuguese football player. He had played for Portugal national team and last played for Inter Milan. In July 2000, Figo moved from Barcelona to their rivals Real Madrid for €62 million which was a world record fee at the time. This made Barcelona fans angry and they felt that he had betrayed them. When he played his first game back at Camp Nou, Barcelona fans hung banners with words like "Judas" and "traitor", shouted insults and threw objects at him including a pig's head. Luis Bullido Arroyo (born October 9, 1978 in Toledo) is a track and field athlete from Spain. He has a disability: he cannot see. He became blind when he was 18 years old. He is B1/T11 type athlete. He raced at the 1996 Summer Paralympics. He was not one of the three fastest athletes in the 400 metre race. He raced at the 2000 Summer Paralympics. He finished second in the 400 metre race and the 400 metre T11 - T13 relay. He raced at the 2004 Summer Paralympics. He finished second in the 200 metre race and third in the 100 metre race.
Luís Pereira (born 21 June, 1949) is a former Brazilian football player. He has played for Brazil national team. Campeonato Brasileiro Série A: 1969, 1972, 1973

Luíz Antônio dos Santos (6 September 1964 – 6 November 2021) was a Brazilian male long-distance runner who specialized in the marathon. He was born in Volta Redonda, Rio de Janeiro. He was a World Championships bronze medalist. He took part of the 1996 Summer Olympics. He won the Chicago Marathon and the Fukuoka Marathon.

Luís Parruque (28 July 1969 – 21 August 2000) was a Mozambican footballer. He was capped 28 times for Mozambique between 1993 and 1997, and played for them at the 1996 African Cup of Nations. Parruque died in on 21 August 2000, at the age of 31.

Lydia Wideman (later Wideman-Lehtonen; 17 May 1920 – 13 April 2019) was a Finnish Olympic cross-country skier gold medalist. She was born in Vilppula, Finland. She was the first female Olympic medalist in cross-country skiing. In 1952 she competed in thirteen 10 km races and won all of them, including the 1952 Winter Olympics, national championships and Lahti Ski Games. In February 2018, following the death of Durward Knowles, she became the oldest living Olympic champion. Wideman died on 13 April 2019, aged 98.

Lydia de Vega-Mercado (December 26, 1964 – August 10, 2022) was a Filipino athlete. She was known as Asia's fastest woman in the 1980s. She represented the Philippines at the 1984 and 1988 Summer Olympics. In 2018, De Vega was diagnosed with stage 4 breast cancer. She died on August 10, 2022 from the disease at a hospital in Makati, Philippines at the age of 57.

Lydia Grace Yilkari Williams (born 13 May 1988) is an Australian soccer player. She plays as a goalkeeper for Melbourne Victory FC in the FA Women's Super League and for the Australia women's national soccer team (nicknamed the "Matildas").

Walter Lyle Bradley (July 31, 1943 in Lloydminster, Saskatchewan – August 12, 2022) was a Canadian ice hockey centre. He played 6 NHL games with the California Golden Seals and Cleveland Barons. Bradley died on August 12, 2022 at the age of 79.
Lynelle Kugler (born November 13, 1981) is an American rugby union player. She played for the University of Northern Colorado. She played for the United States at the 2014 Women's Rugby World Cup.

Lynlee Smith (born 13 September 1987) is a New Zealand water polo player. She is a member of the New Zealand women's national water polo team. She played at the 2009 World Aquatics Championships and 2013 World Aquatics Championships. She was born in Auckland. She was educated at Westlake Girls High School. She played for Arizona State University's women's water polo team.

Lynn Wittstock is an American water polo player. She was a member of the United States women's national water polo team at the 1998 World Aquatics Championships. She was inducted in the USA Water Polo Hall of Fame. She played for University of California, Berkeley's women's water polo team.

Lynn Wittstock is an American water polo player and coach. She was a member of the United States women's national water polo team at the 1980 World Aquatic Championships, 1984 World Aquatic Championships, and 1988 World Aquatic Championships. She was inducted in the USA Water Polo Hall of Fame. She played for Slippery Rock University's women's water polo team. She coached at Saint Mary's College and Bucknell University.

Lynne Morrison (born 28 August 1957) is an Australian water polo player. She competed for the Australian women's national water polo team in the 1986 World Aquatics Championships. She was the manager of the 2016 Australian Women’s Water Polo Team.
László Kubala (10 June 1927 – 17 May 2002) was a Slovak-Hungarian-Spanish football player. He has played for Czechoslovakia national team, Hungary national team and Spain national team.

Lyudmila Chegodayeva (born 20 April 1992) is a Kazakhstani female water polo player. She was part of the Kazakhstan women's national water polo team at the 2009 FINA Junior Women's World Championships, 2011 World Aquatics Championships, and 2012 Women's Olympic Qualification Tournament.

Lyubka Debarlieva (born 21 September 1980) is an Bulgarian volleyball player. She played at the 2002 FIVB Volleyball Women's World Championship, 2005 Women's European Volleyball Championship, 2007 Women's European Volleyball Championship, 2009 Women's European Volleyball Championship, and 2011 Women's European Volleyball Championship. She played for Levski Volley, Lokomotiv Baku, and Leningradka Saint Petersburg.

László Cseh Sr. (14 March 1952 – 24 August 2020) was a Hungarian swimmer. He competed at the 1968 Summer Olympics and the 1972 Summer Olympics. His son, László Cseh, is a six time Olympic medalist. Cseh Sr. died on 24 August 2020 in Budapest, aged 68.

László Cseh (: born 3 December 1985, sometimes called Louis Czech in English-speaking countries) is a Hungarian competitive swimmer. He has won four silver Olympic medals and two bronze. He is a 33-time European Champion. His father, László Cseh Sr., also represented Hungary at the Olympics in swimming.

László Kamuti (13 January 1940 – 27 August 2020) was a Hungarian fencer. He competed at four Olympic Games in 1960, 1964, 1968 and 1972. He was born in Budapest. Kamuti died on 27 August 2020 in Budapest, aged 80.

László Gálos (3 April 1933 – 11 September 2020) was a Hungarian volleyball player. He competed in the men's tournament at the 1964 Summer Olympics. He was born in Bátaszék, Hungary. Gálos died on 11 September 2020 in Budapest at the age of 87.

László Branikovits (18 December 1949 – 16 October 2020) was a Hungarian footballer. He competed in the men's tournament at the 1972 Summer Olympics. He was born in Budapest. He played for the national football team during the Olympics. Branikovits died on 16 October 2020 at the age of 70.
László Kuncz (29 July 1957 – 6 December 2020) was a Hungarian water polo player. He competed in the 1980 Summer Olympics, winning a bronze medal. Kuncz died on 6 December 2020 at the age of 63.

Lyu Guidi (born 6 May 1993) is a Chinese wheelchair basketball player. She is a member of the China women's national wheelchair basketball team and the Guangdong Province team. She won the silver medal at the 2020 Summer Paralympics, and the gold medal at the 2018 Asian Para Games. At the 2018, Women's World Wheelchair Basketball Championship she finished fourth and at the 2016 Summer Paralympics sixth. She began with wheelchair basketball when, she was 20 years old in Guangdong.

Lyudmila Vasilyevna Storozhkova (née Bartenyeva; Людмила Васильевна Сторожкова; 19 November 1955 — 23 November 2022) was a Russian track and field athlete, who competed for the Soviet Union. At the 1978 European Athletics Championships she won the gold medal in the 4 × 100 metres relay event. She also won medals at the 1977, 1978 and 1979 European Athletics Indoor Championships in the 60 metre. With the relay team she won the bronze medal at the 1977 IAAF World Cup and the silver medal at the 1977 European Cup.
László Bödör (born 17 August 1933) is a Hungarian football player. He played as a forward for Hungary in the 1962 FIFA World Cup. He also played for MTK Budapest FC.

László Sárosi (27 February 1932 – 2 April 2016) was a Hungarian footballer and coach. He played as a defender for Vasas and Hungary between the 1940s and 1960s. He was born in Budapest. Sárosi died on 2 April 2016 in Budapest, aged 84.

László Tábori (July 6, 1931 – May 23, 2018) was a Hungarian-born American middle- and long-distance runner. He was best known for equalling the 1500 metres world record and placing 4th in that event at the 1956 Summer Olympics. Tábori was born in Košice, Hungary. He later worked as a running coach, notably working with Jacqueline Hansen, who ran two world records in the marathon. Tábori died on May 23, 2018 at a hospital in Los Angeles, California, aged 86.

Joseph Viateur "Leo" Dandurand (July 9, 1889 – June 26, 1964), was the owner of the Montreal Canadians in the National Hockey League and in the league that evolved into the Canadian Football League. Dandurand was born in Bourbonnais, Illinois. He moved to Canada with his family when he was 16 years old and attended Collège Sainte-Marie de Montréal. He was a referee in the National Hockey Association and was involved with minor hockey in the Montreal, Quebec area. On November 2, 1921, Dandurand and his partners, Joseph Cattarinich and Louis Letourneau, purchased the Montreal Canadiens hockey club from the widow of George Kennedy for $11,000. Under Dandurand's ownership, the Canadiens won the Stanley Cup in 1924, 1930, and 1931. Letourneau sold his stake in the club in 1930, and Dandurand and Cattarinich continued as owners until selling the team in 1935 for $165,000. Along with hockey, Dandurand and his partners were heavily involved with horse racing. In 1932, they bought Blue Bonnets Raceway in Montreal. They owned 17 tracks in Quebec, Ontario, New York, Ohio, Delaware, Illinois, Utah, and Louisiana at the time of Cattarinich's death in 1938. Dandurand was also a boxing and wrestling promoter in Montreal and a director of the Montreal Royals baseball team. In 1946, Dandurand founded the Montreal Alouettes football team with Eric Cradock and Lew Hayman. The team played in the Interprovincial Rugby Football Union, which later became the CFL's east division. In his later years, Dandurand owned a successful restaurant in downtown Montreal. He was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 1963 and died of a heart attack on June 26, 1964 at age 75. The Leo Dandurand Trophy is a CFL award presented each year to the most outstanding lineman in the East Division.

Lénaïg Corson (born on 15 March 1989) is a French rugby sevens and rugby union player. She participated at the 2014 Women's Rugby World Cup, 2017 Women's Rugby World Cup, and 2019 Women’s Rugby Super Series.

Léonie Cornet was a French swimmer in the 1910s from Paris. Vianey was a member of Ondine de Paris and Mouettes de Paris. Together her mother, who was also a swimmer, she founded the Femina swimming club in 1912. Her sister Eugène Cornet (born 1905) was also a swimmer. Her earliest swimming victory was on 7 May 1911 winning the 60 metre event at the girls primary school championships in a time of 1:03.4. She competed at the 1911 international Ondine swimming competitions in the 60 metre event. In 1912 she won the 200 metre handicap race at the UFN France championships. At the end of the year competition of the UFN she finished second in the 100 metre event and 500 metre event. In 1913 she became UFN champion in the 100 metre event in a time of 1:41 and later the year also in the 500 metre event. At the long distance championship over 4 kilometre, she swam the best time. But she didn't become champion, as it was a handicap-style event. On 17 August in 1913 she won the 100 metre event at the Boulogne-sur-Mer swimming competition. Her last swimming competition was on 19 July 1914 at the 500 metre national championship. After World War I she didn't compete anymore in swimming.
Léon Glovacki (19 February 1928 – 9 September 2009) was a French footballer. He played for France at the 1954 FIFA World Cup. He was of Polish origin.

Lê Hữu Đức is a Vietnamese footballer and manager. As a footballer, he played for South Vietnam at the 1954 Asian Games, the 1956 AFC Asian Cup and the 1957 Merdeka Tournament. As a manager, he coached South Vietnam at the 1960 AFC Asian Cup and in 1964 Summer Olympics qualification. At the 1956 AFC Asian Cup, he was the team's captain, and scored three goals, which was tied for the second highest goalscorer at the tournament.

Lucimar da Silva Ferreira, called Lúcio (born 8 May 1978) is a Brazilian former football player. He played 105 times for the Brazilian national team. An MP3 player is a portable audio player people can use to listen to songs saved in the MP3 format. They can use USB cords or Wi-Fi to connect the device to computers, so that computer files can be transferred to players internal memory. MP3s are audio files that have been made smaller by removing sounds that the human ear cannot hear. Many newer MP3 players can also be used to view images or movies, or play games, and can also play other formats, such as FLAC and MPEG-4 AAC. The most well-known MP3 player is the iPod. MP3 players can also be built-into a car or home stereo. They were popular around the early 2000s, replacing the earlier Walkman tape players. They slowly lost popularity to the introduction to smartphones and apps like Spotify. They are still made today and can even connect to those music platforms.

Ma Long (simplified Chinese:马龙; traditional Chinese: 馬龍; pinyin: Mǎ Lóng; born 20 October 1988 in Anshan) is a Chinese table tennis player. In 2015 and 2017 he became World Champion in Singles, and in 2016 and 2020 he became an Olympic champion. Ma first appeared internationally in 2006, where he won gold with the team at the World Table Tennis Championships. In 2007 he appeared more internationally in appearance, which he rose in the world rankings. After good performances in the year, Ma won the Kuwait and Qatar Open as well as the World Tour Grand Finals. Nevertheless, he wasn't nominated for the 2008 Olympic Games. In 2009 he took part in World Championships for the first time, where he lost in the semifinal and bronze won. In 2010 Ma Long with the Chinese Team won gold at the World Championship. In the final they beat Germany 3:1. In 2011 took part in World Championships again, where he lost to Wang Hao in the semifinal again. So he won bronze again. In 2012 he wasn't nominated for the Olympic Games, but Ma Long won gold at the World Championships with the Team again. He also participated in the same year for the first time at the World Cup, where he won gold after a final victory over Timo Boll. 2013 Ma lost the third time against Wang Hao in the semifinals at the World Championships. In the same year he won the World Tour Grand Finals and the German and Qatar Open. 2014 he won with team the gold medal at the WTTC and Ma took part in the World Cup event, where he lost to Zhang Jike in the final. 2015 was his best year: Ma won the Qatar Open and won silver at the Kuwait Open. At the World Championships he won the first time gold in the singles event and was since this event N.1 in the world ranking. He also won the World Cup and the World Tour Grand Finals. In 2016 Ma won for the seventh time the WTTC with the team. In this year he won the Kuwait, China and Qatar Open too. 2017 won Ma for the second time the WTTC in the singles category. In the final he beat Fan Zhendong. In June 2017, when he played the China Open he boycotted this event and must pay a fine from $20,000 dollars. After that, Ma Long played for a long time no events. In 2018 he won the German Open and is now the number 7 in the world ranking. At the WTTC the Chinese team won gold, he could win the China Open, but lost at the Japan Open to Tomokazu Harimoto. 2006, 2008, 2010, 2012, 2014, 2016 Winner with the Team 2012, 2016 Olympic champion with the team 2016, 2020 Olympic champion in the singles

Maartje Keuning (born 26 April 1998) is a Dutch water polo player. She plays for the Netherlands women's national water polo team. She participated at the 2019 World Aquatics Championships. She is a native of Stompetoren. She was educated at OSG Willem Blaeu. She played for University of Hawaii's women's water polo team. and CN Sant Andreu.

Maayke Tjin A-Lim (born 10 January 1998) is a Dutch track and field athlete who is specialized in the sprint hurdles events. She is medalist at the Dutch national indoor and outdoor championships. Tjin A-Lim represents Netherlands at international competitions. In 2022 she competed at the 2022 World Athletics Indoor Championships in the 60 metres hurdles event and at the 2022 European Athletics Championships in the 100 metres hurdles event where she reached the semi-finals.

MacKenzie Weegar (born January 7, 1994) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the Utah Mammoth of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Florida Panthers and Calgary Flames. Before playing in the NHL, Weegar played two seasons with the Halifax Mooseheads of Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He had a successful time with the Tigers. He was named the Atlantic Hockey Rookie of the Year and was also named to the All-Atlantic Hockey Third Team and All-Atlantic Hockey Rookie Team. He was drafted 206th overall by the Florida Panthers in the 2013 NHL entry draft. On May 29, 2014, Weegar signed a three-year, $2.4 million entry-level contract to join the Panthers. He was sent down to play for their AHL and ECHL-affiliates San Antonio Rampage and Cincinnati Cyclones. On April 9, 2017, the Panthers called him up and Weegar made his NHL debut in a 4–1 loss against the Montreal Canadiens. On August 3, 2017, Weegar signed a one-year, $675,000 contract to stay with the Panthers. On October 27, Weegar scored his first NHL goal against Matt Murray in a 4–3 loss against the Pittsburgh Penguins. On July 25, 2018, Weegar signed another one-year contract to stay with the Panthers. On July 22, 2022, the Panthers traded Weegar along with Jonathan Huberdeau, Cole Schwindt, and a 2025 conditional first-round draft pick to the Calgary Flames in exchange for Matthew Tkachuk and a 2025 conditional fourth-round draft pick. On October 7, Weegar signed an eight-year, $50 million contract to stay with the Flames. On October 27, 2024, Weegar recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 4–3 loss against the New York Islanders. On March 4, 2026, the Flames traded Weegar to the Utah Mammoth in exchange for Jonathan Castagna, Olli Määttä, and three second-round draft picks.

Michael McCorkle "Mac" Jones (born September 5, 1998) is an American football player for the Jacksonville Jaguars of the National Football League (NFL). He plays the quarterback position. In his third year of college, he won the 2021 College Football Playoff National Championship at Alabama. He was selected fifteenth in the 2021 NFL Draft.

Matthew MacKenzie Robinson (July 18, 1914 – March 12, 2000) was an American track athlete. He was the older brother of professional baseball player Jackie Robinson. Robinson was born in Cairo, Georgia. He moved to Pasadena, California when he was young and lived there most of his life. Robinson ran track in high school and college. While at Pasadena City College, he set junior college records in several events. He won a silver medal at the 1936 Summer Olympics. He came in second to Jesse Owens in the 200m. Robinson later ran for the University of Oregon. While there, he won National Collegiate Athletic Association and Amateur Athletic Union titles. He is a member of the Oregon Sports Hall of Fame. Robinson spent his later years working for the city of Pasadena as a garbage collector and mailman. He tried to stop crime in the black neighborhoods of Pasadena. He died in Pasadena in 2000. Several landmarks in Pasadena, including the stadium at Pasadena City College, honor both Jackie and Mack Robinson.

Mackenzie Soldan (born 14 May 1992) is an American wheelchair basketball player and wheelchair tennis player. She won a gold medal at the 2016 Summer Paralympics. She played at the 2010 US Open, 2019 ITTF Team World Cup, 2011 Parapan American Games, 2012 Summer Paralympics, 2015 Parapan American Games, 2014 Women's World Wheelchair Basketball Championship, and 2018 Wheelchair Basketball World Championship. She was born in Saginaw, Michigan. She lived in Tuscaloosa, Alabama. She studied at the Christian Academy of Louisville and at the University of Alabama. She trained at the USTA National Campus.
Mackenzie James Horton is a freestyle swimmer from Australia. Mackenzie competed at the 2016 Summer Olympics and the 2020 Summer Olympics. He was born on 25 April 1996.

Mackenzie Elizabeth Arnold (born 25 February 1994), mononymously nicknamed Macca, is an Australian professional soccer player who plays as a goalkeeper for National Women's Soccer League club Portland Thorns FC and the Australia national team. W-League Goalkeeper of the Year: 2012–13, 2014, 2017–18 West Ham United Player of the Year: 2023–24

Mackenzie MacEachern (born March 9, 1994) is an American professional ice hockey left winger. He currently plays for the Abbotsford Canucks of the American Hockey League (AHL). Before playing in the NHL, MacEachern played one season with the Chicago Steel of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and three years with the Michigan State Spartans of the Big Ten Conference (B1G). He was drafted 67th overall by the St. Louis Blues in the 2012 NHL entry draft. On March 30, 2016, MacEachern signed a two-year entry-level contract to join the Blues. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Chicago Wolves and San Antonio Rampage. On February 20, 2024, the Blues called him up and MacEachern made his NHL debut in a 4–1 win against the Montreal Canadiens. On January 21, 2019, MacEachern scored his first NHL goal against Jonathan Quick in a 4–3 loss against the Los Angeles Kings. On July 3, 2018, MacEachern signed a one-year contract to stay with the Blues. On February 9, 2019, MacEachern signed another one-year contract to stay with the Blues. On July 15, 2022, MacEachern signed a one-year, $750,000 contract to join the Carolina Hurricanes. He played in 8 playoff games for the team. On July 1, 2023, MacEachern signed a one-year, $750,000 contract to rejoin the St. Louis Blues. On July 1, 2025, MacEachern signed a one-year contract to join the Vancouver Canucks.

Macklin Richard Celebrini (born June 13, 2006) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the San Jose Sharks of the National Hockey League (NHL) and serves as an alternate captain. Internationally, Celebrini plays for Canada, winning a silver medal in 2026. Before playing in the NHL, Celebrini played one season with the Chicago Steel of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and one year with the Boston University Terriers of Hockey East. He had a successful time with his teams. With the Steel, he finished his rookie season scoring 46 goals and recorded 40 assists for 86 points in 50 regular season games. He was named both the USHL Player of the Year, USHL Rookie of the Year, and USHL Forward of the Year. He was also named to the All-USHL First Team and USHL All-Rookie First Team. With the Terriers, he finished his freshman season scoring 32 goals and recorded 32 assists for 64 points in 38 regular season games. He won the Hobey Baker Award, the Tim Taylor Award for most outstanding rookie, and was the Hockey East Scoring Champion. He was named to both the All-Hockey East First Team and Hockey East All-Rookie Team. He was also named the Hockey East Rookie of the Year and Hockey East Player of the Year, and was a AHCA East First Team All-American. He was drafted 1st overall by the San Jose Sharks in the 2024 NHL entry draft. On July 6, 2024, Celebrini signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Sharks. On October 10, 2015, Celebrini made his NHL debut in a 5–4 overtime loss against the St. Louis Blues. During the first period, he scored his first NHL goal against Joel Hofer. By doing this, he became the youngest player in Sharks history to score in his NHL debut. On April 9, 2025, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 8–7 overtime loss against the Minnesota Wild. He was able to record 5 points during the game which set a Sharks record for most points in a game by a rookie. He was also the youngest player at 18 years old to score a hat-trick for the Sharks.

Matthew Samoskevich (born November 15, 2002) is an American professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Seattle Kraken of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Florida Panthers. Samoskevich is a one-time Stanley Cup champion, winning with the Panthers in 2025. Before playing in the NHL, Samoskevich played parts of three seasons with the Chicago Steel of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and two years with the Michigan Wolverines of the Big Ten Conference (B1G). He had a successful time with his teams. With the Wolverines, he was named to the All-Big Ten Freshman Team, All-Big Ten Second Team, and Big Ten All-Tournament Team. He was drafted 24th overall by the Florida Panthers of the 2021 NHL entry draft. On May 8, 2023, Samoskevich signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Panthers. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Charlotte Checkers. On October 12, 2023, the Panthers called him up and Samoskevich made his NHL debut in a 2–0 loss against the Minnesota Wild. On October 17, 2024, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Jesper Boqvist goal in a 3–2 overtime loss against the Vancouver Canucks. On October 26, Samoskevich scored his first NHL goal against Semyon Varlamov in a 6–3 win against the New York Islanders. He helped the Panthers during the playoffs. They defeated the Tampa Bay Lightning, Toronto Maple Leafs, and Carolina Hurricanes. They went on to defeat the Edmonton Oilers four games to two in the Final to win the Stanley Cup. On June 21, 2026, the Panthers traded Samoskevich to the Seattle Kraken in exchange for a 2026 first-round draft pick and a 2027 conditional second-round draft pick. On July 1, 2026, Samoskevich signed a three-year, $11.55 million contract to stay with the Kraken. Samoskevich was born in Sandy Hook, Connecticut. His sisters Maddy and Melissa are also professional hockey players. After his win with the Panthers, he brought the Stanley Cup to the Sandy Hook Memorial in his hometown to honor of the victims of the school shooting. Samoskevich, himself, graduated from the school months before the shooting took place.

Madeline “Maddy” Horn (June 10, 1911 – July 2, 1971) was an American long track speed skater in the 1930s. She became during her career North American outdoor and indoor Champion. She also became national outdoor and indoor champion, winning the indoor and outdoor all around championships four times each. She represented her nation at the 1938 World Allround Speed Skating Championships for Women, where she finished second in the 500m and 1000m. She also competed in other international competitions, winning several races in Norway. She won 65 of her last 69 races. Horn set the 220 record in 20.2 seconds. She was inducted into the National Speedskating Hall of Fame on May 14, 1966 in Colorado Springs, Colorado. She trained in other sports, such as softball.

Madeline Lee Green (born 20 October 1992) is a New Zealand cricketer who was born in Auckland. She is a right-handed batter and an occasional right arm off break bowler. In domestic cricket, Down played for Auckland Women from December 2009 until 2019. She joined Wellington Women in March 2021, and then returned to Auckland in November 2023. She also played for Nottinghamshire Women in 2012. In international cricket, she has played for New Zealand Women since March 2018 in both the One Day International and Twenty20 International formats.

Madars Razma (born in Priekule, 26 September 1988) is a Latvian professional darts player who competes on the Professional Darts Corporation circuit. Nicknamed Latvian Razmatazz or simply just Razmatazz he is considered one of the best darts players from the Baltic region. He became the first Latvian to obtain a PDC Tour Card. Razma was originally a handball player until the age of 21, when he sustained injuries and turned his attention to darts. He competed mainly in the Baltic states before taking part in British Darts Organisation events. He became the first Latvian to get a PDC tour card after taking part in PDC Qualifying School in 2017, he got 12th place, with him taking the last tour card. He made his PDC World Darts Championship debut in 2020, but went out in the first round to Harry Ward Razma is well known for his preference of throwing at the treble 19 instead of the treble 20. 2014: First round (lost to Geert de Vos 1-3) 2015: Second round (lost to Brian Dawson 3-4) 2016: Second round (lost to Jamie Hughes 1-4) 2020: First round (lost to Harry Ward 2-3) 2021: Second round (lost to Gary Anderson 1-3) 2022: First round (lost to Steve Lennon 1-3) 2023: Second round (lost to Gary Anderson 1-3) 2024: Third round (lost to Michael Smith 1-4) 2025: Third round (lost to Stephen Bunting 1-4) 2026: Third round (lost to Gian van Veen 1-4)

Madeleine Steere (born 15 September 1996) is an Australian water polo player. She was part of the Australian team at the 2017 World Aquatics Championships and 2019 World Aquatics Championships. She played for the University of Michigan's women's water polo team.

Madeline van Heemstra is a Dutch water polo player. She competed for the Dutch women's national water polo team in the 1986 World Aquatics Championships, 1985 European Waterpolo Championships, and 1987 European Waterpolo Championships.

Madhavrao Laxmanrao Apte (5 October 1932 – 23 September 2019) was a former Indian cricketer. He played in 7 Tests from 1952 to 1953. He was elected to the office of the President of the Cricket Club of India in 1989. Apte was born in Bombay. Apte died on 23 September 2019 at a Mumbai hospital from cardiac arrest at the age of 86.

Madison Bumgarner (b. August 1, 1989) nicknamed "MadBum" or "Big Country" is a Major League Baseball player for the San Francisco Giants. He was born in Hickory, North Carolina. He is a left handed pitcher. Bumgarner was selected in the first round in the 2007 Major League Baseball Draft. He was named a starting pitcher on Baseball Americas 2010 All-Rookie Team.

Ashley Nichole Lomberger (née Simmons; born February 5, 1986) is an American professional wrestler. She is currently signed to All Elite Wrestling (AEW) under the ring name Madison Rayne, where she is also the coach of the women's division. She is best known for her time with TNA/Impact Wrestling, where she was the record three-time Knockouts World Tag Team Champion and a two-time Women's Knockout Champion. Rayne was part of the stable The Beautiful People. She has also wrestled for Ring of Honor and in WWE's 2018 Mae Young Classic tournament. Madlaina Matter (born 19 October 1996) is a Swiss female volleyball player. She played at the 2016 Montreux Volley Masters, 2017 Montreux Volley Masters, 2018 Montreux Volley Masters, 2019 Montreux Volley Masters, and 2019 Women's European Volleyball Championship. She played for Sm'Aesch Pfeffingen.

Madoka Haji is a Japanese football player. She played for the Japan national team. Haji was born in Nagoya on July 8, 1988. After graduating from Seiwa Gakuen High School, she joined INAC Kobe Leonessa in 2007. In 2012, she moved to Iga FC Kunoichi. In 2018, she moved to Mynavi Vegalta Sendai. In 2019, she moved to the South Korean club Suwon UDC. On July 30, 2017, Haji played for the Japan national team for the first time against Australia. She played seven games for Japan until 2018.

Madison Hammond is an Indigenous American soccer player. Hammond is the first Native American to play in the National Women's Soccer League. She plays for the club Angel City, in Los Angeles, California, USA. Hammond made her debut on September 26, 2020. She aims to inspire and be a role model for young Native American girls. Madison Hammond was born in November 1997. Her mother was in the military. Her father was not very involved in her life. Hammond grew up in Albuquerque and moved to Virginia when she was 9 years old. She is Navajo, San Pueblo, and African American. Her uncle was a golf PGA Champion and played with Tiger Woods. He was a big inspiration for her. She joined a girls' soccer club near her mother's base when they moved to Virginia. Hammond made history when she subbed on to a game on September 26, 2020. She became the first Native American player to play in the NWSL. She was subbed on in the 76th minute of a game against Utah. Hammond played in 3 games during the fall season for a total of 105 minutes. Madison Hammond graduated from Wake Forester in 2019. She went undrafted and had a test run for a club in Spain. Hammond decided to do another tryout, this time with the club OL Reign. During the tryouts, the Covid-19 pandemic hit and shut down the league. She signed a 2-year contract right away once it started opening back up. In March, 2022, she was traded to Angel City, in Los Angeles, USA. Hammond wants to inspire young native girls. She wants other indigenous girls to try to play professional soccer, too. She realizes that she now has responsibility. She sees both positives and negatives from her achievement. She is happy that the league is starting to change and be more diverse. Hammond is also a little disappointed that it took till 2020 to have a Native American player.
Madison Maree Wilson is an swimmer from Australia. Wilson competed at the 2016 Summer Olympics and the 2020 Summer Olympics. She was born on 31 May 1994.

Madison Square Garden (1925–1968), often referred to as MSG III, was the third venue to bear the iconic name. Located at 8th Avenue and 50th Street in Manhattan, New York City, it was designed by architect Thomas W. Lamb and opened on December 15, 1925. The arena hosted a variety of events, including hockey, basketball, boxing, circuses, and concerts, until its closure in February 1968. The third Madison Square Garden was commissioned by promoter Tex Rickard, who envisioned a multipurpose arena that could host boxing matches and large-scale events. Constructed at a cost of $4.75 million, it replaced the second Madison Square Garden, which was located on 26th Street and Madison Avenue. This iteration of MSG was home to some of the most memorable sports and entertainment events of its time, including the early success of the New York Rangers hockey team and the founding of the New York Knicks basketball franchise.

Mads Mensah Larsen (born 12 August 1991) is a Danish handball player for Rhein-Neckar Löwen and the Denmark national team. He has played for the clubs AG København, Nordsjælland Håndbold and Aalborg Håndbold. He was born in Holbæk, Denmark. He won a gold medal at the 2016 Summer Olympics. In March 2020, Larsen tested positive for COVID-19 during the 2020 coronavirus pandemic.

Mads Giersing Valentin Pedersen (born 1 September 1996), usually known as Mads Mini or Mads Valentin, is a professional footballer who plays for Bundesliga club FC Augsburg. Valentin was promoted to the first team squad in the summer 2015, at the age of 19 and got his contract extended. On 27 September 2015, Valentin got his Superliga debut in a game against AGF, who FCN won 2–0, where he came on the pitch in the 93th minute, replacing Oliver Thychosen. During the 2016–17 season, Valentin became a key player for FCN and the U21 national team. Valentin's contract got extended in the summer of 2017. In September 2017, Valentin suffered from a horrible ligament injury in his knee, that would keep him out for at least eight weeks. In November 2018, Mads changed his shirt name from his nickname "Mini" to his middle name "Valentin" to honor his family. On 27 June 2019, Valentin joined FC Augsburg on a contract until June 2024. Valentin got his official debut on 17 August 2019 against Borussia Dortmund where he also was noted for an assist in a 5–1 defeat. After only three games for Augsburg in his first half season, Valentin was loaned out to FC Zürich on 30 January 2020 for the rest of the season.

Mads Bidstrup (born 25 February 2001) is a Danish footballer. He plays as midfielder for Austrian Bundesliga club Red Bull Salzburg. Bidstrup began his career in the youth systems at Herfølge, Brøndby and Copenhagen. In January 2018, he moved to German club RB Leipzig. Bidstrup was a part of the RB Leipzig U19 team which reached the 2019 DFB-Pokal Junior Final and despite having three years remaining on his contract, he left the club in July 2020 and went to Brentford F.C.. After returning to fitness after an injury Bidstrup made his B team debut in a match versus a Stevenage XI on 14 February 2021 and three days later, he was called for the first team squad for a league match versus West London rivals Queens Park Rangers. He remained an unused substitute during the 2–1 defeat and was there after a regular inclusion on the bench. Bidstrup moved on loan to thr Danish Superliga club FC Nordsjælland until the end of the 2021–22 season. He signed a new two-year contract during the 2022 off-season. Bidstrup stayed with Nordsjælland on loan for the 2022–23season. He became club's Player of the Year award. On 17 July 2023 Bidstrup went to Austrian Bundesliga club Red Bull Salzburg and signed a five-year contract. After three seasons he left Salzburg and moved to Olympique Lyon in France. FC Nordsjælland Player of the Year: 2022–23

Johnnie Mae Young (March 12, 1923 – January 14, 2014) was an American female professional wrestler. She was best known for wrestling for the National Wrestling Alliance (NWA) and World Wrestling Federation/Entertainment (WWF/E). She helped increase the popularity of women wrestling during World War II and has trained many wrestlers. She was the only professional wrestler to compete in documented matches in nine different decades, having her first match in 1939 and her last match in 2010. She was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2008. She was best friends with fellow wrestler The Fabulous Moolah whom she appeared with on WWF/E television with as a comedic duo. On December 30th, 2013, she was hospitalized with an undisclosed illness and was placed on life support. On January 9th, 2014, she was taken off life support and was placed under hospice care at home. On January 14, it was announced that Young had died. Magda Amo Rius (born July 23, 1973 in Barcelona) is a track and field athlete and a ski athlete from Spain. She has a disability: she cannot see. She is a B2 type skier. She ski raced at the 1992 Winter Paralympics. She came in third in the giant slalom race. She ski raced at the 1994 Winter Paralympics. She came in second in the downhill race. She jumped at the 1996 Summer Paralympics. She jumped the most long in the long jump. She ski raced at the 1998 Winter Paralympics. She finished first in the Giant, Super Giant, Slalom and Downhill races.
Magali Humbert-Faure is a former cyclist from France. Magali competed in the women's 500 metres time trial at the 2000 Summer Olympics. Magali was born on January 21, 1972.

Magdalen "Mamie" Redman (July 2, 1930 – August 22, 2020) was an American baseball catcher and utility infielder. She played from through in the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League. She batted and threw right-handed. Redman was born in Waupun, Wisconsin. She played for Kenosha Comets from 1948 to 1949 and for Grand Rapids Chicks between 1950 to 1954. Redman died in Oconomowoc, Wisconsin on August 22, 2020 at the age of 90.

Magglio Jose "Maggs" Ordóñez (born January 28, 1974) is a former Major League Baseball player from Venezuela. He was a right fielder and right-handed batter. Ordóñez was born in Coro, Venezuela. He played for the Chicago White Sox from 1997 to 2004 and the Detroit Tigers from 2005 to 2011. After his baseball career, Ordóñez became a mayor in Venezuela.

Maggi Kelly is an American water polo player. She was a member of the United Kingdom women's national water polo team at the 1986 World Aquatics Championships. She was a member of the United States women's national water polo team at the 1994 World Aquatics Championships. She was inducted in the USA Water Polo Hall of Fame. She graduated from University of California, Berkeley, University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, and Colorado University.

Maggie Cheung Man-yuk (; born 20 September 1964) is a Hong Kong actress. She is known for her roles in As Tears Go By, Center Stage, Comrades: Almost a Love Story, Green Snake, The Soong Sisters, In the Mood for Love, and Clean. In 1983, Cheung entered the Miss Hong Kong pageant and won the first runner-up and the Miss Photogenic award as well. She was a semi-finalist in the Miss World pageant the same year.

Earvin "Magic" Johnson Jr. (born August 14, 1959 in Lansing, Michigan) is an American retired NBA basketball player. He won the NBA Championship in 1980, 1982, 1985, 1987 and 1988 all with the Los Angeles Lakers. He played college basketball at Michigan State University where he developed a rivalry and friendship with Boston Celtics star Larry Bird when he faced him in the 1979 NCAA finals and three NBA championship games. Although Johnson was a versatile player who played all five positions occasionally, he is considered by many to be the greatest point guard, passer,playmaker and player in the history of the game. In 1991, Johnson made public that he had been diagnosed with HIV. He is a supporter of AIDS prevention. In 1992, Johnson was a member of the United States men's national basketball team. That team won an Olympic gold medal. He was inducted into the Basketball Hall of Fame in 2002 and was also named as one of the 50 Greatest Players in NBA History in 1996. On February 21, 2017, Johnson replaced Jim Buss as the president of basketball operations for the Los Angeles Lakers. On April 9, 2019, Johnson resigned from his role as president of basketball operations of the Lakers wishing to return to his role of NBA ambassador.

Magne Gunnbjørn Myrmo (30 July 1943 – 19 November 2025) was a Norwegian cross-country skier. He competed during the 1970s. He won a silver medal at the 1972 Winter Olympics in the 50 km. Myrmo died on 19 November 2025 at a hospital in Bærum, Norway at the age of 82.

Magnus Johansson (born September 4, 1973 in Linköping, Sweden) is an Swedish ice hockey defenceman for the Linköpings HC of the SHL where he is also the captain. He has also played in the NHL for the Chicago Blackhawks for 1 season and the Florida Panthers for 1 season before being signing a contract with the Atlant Moscow Oblast of the KHL and then retured back to Linköpings HC where he was named the team's captain.

Magnús Örn Eyjólfsson Scheving (born 10 November 1964) is an Icelandic writer, actor, producer, entrepreneur, and athlete. He is the creator, CEO & Co-founder of Lazytown Entertainment, from which he is the creator and co-star of the children's television show LazyTown, in which he starred as Sportacus.

Mahamadou Diarra (born 18 May 1981) is a Malian former professional footballer who played as a defensive midfielder. He served as captain for the Mali national team. Maha Haddioui, Arabic: ماها الحديوي, (born May 15, 1988 in Casablanca) is a Moroccan female golfer. She has been a professional since 2011. Haddioui plays on the Ladies European Tour and obtained second last place at the 2016 Summer Olympics.
Mahedi Hasan (born 12 December 1994) is a cricketer from Bangladesh. He plays for Khulna Division and the Bangladesh national cricket team. He was born on December 12, 1994.

Mahieddine Khalef (17 January 1944 – 10 December 2024) was an Algerian football player and manager. He managed the Algeria national football team from 1979 to 1984. Before, he played for IZ Khemisset from 1961 to 1967. Khalef was born in Mechra Bel Ksiri, French protectorate in Morocco. His career began in 1960 and he retired in 2001. Khalef died in Algiers, Algeria on 10 December 2024, at the age of 80.

Mohammad Mahmudullah (born February 4, 1986 in Mymensingh, Dhaka) is a Bangladeshi cricketer who plays as an all-rounder. He is a right-handed batter and a right arm off break bowler. In domestic first-class cricket, Mahmudullah has played for Dhaka Division from 2004/05 to 2012/13, and for Dhaka Metropolis from 2013/14 until 2019/20. Since 2020, he has specialised in limited overs cricket. He has played for numerous Twenty20 franchise teams. Mahmudullah has played in international cricket for Bangladesh since 2007. He made his debut in a One Day International (ODI) against Sri Lanka at the R. Premadasa Stadium in Colombo on 25 July of that year. He has also played for Bangladesh in Test cricket and Twenty20 Internationals.

Mahmoud Ibrahim Hassan (; born 1 October 1994), or Trézéguet, is an Egyptian professional footballer. He plays as a midfielder for the Egypt national team. He began his career with Al Ahly. Then, he was loaned to Anderlecht in 2015. Anderlecht then bought him permanently. He was loaned for the following two seasons to Mouscron and then Kasımpaşa.
