Before playing in the NHL, Marchment played one season with the Erie Otters, one season with the Hamilton Bulldogs, and one season with the Mississauga Steelheads of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was not drafted by an NHL team. On March 17, 2018, Marchment signed a two-year, $1.85 million entry-level contract to join the Toronto Maple Leafs of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was sent down to play for their AHL and ECHL-affiliates Toronto Marlies and Orlando Solar Bears. On January 2, 2020, the Leafs called him up and Marchment made his NHL debut in a 6–3 win against the Winnipeg Jets. On January 6, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Frédérik Gauthier goal in a 6–4 loss against the Edmonton Oilers. On February 19, 2020, the Leafs traded Marchment to the Florida Panthers in exchange for Denis Malgin. On March 4, 2021, Marchment scored his first NHL goal against Pekka Rinne in a 5–4 win against the Nashville Predators. He played parts of two seasons with the Panthers. On July 13, 2022, Marchment signed a four-year, $18 million contract to join the Dallas Stars. He played parts of three seasons with the Stars. On June 19, 2025, the Stars traded Marchment to the Seattle Kraken in exchange for 2025 fourth-round draft pick and a 2026 third-round draft pick. He played 29 regular season games with the Kraken, scoring 4 goals and recording 9 assists for 13 points. On December 20, 2025, the Kraken traded Marchment to the Columbus Blue Jackets in exchange for 2027 fourth-round draft pick and the New York Rangers' 2026 third-round draft pick which the Jackets held. Marchment's father Bryan Marchment and cousin Kennedy Marchment are also professional hockey players. Bryan played 18 seasons in the NHL. Kennedy plays for the Montreal Victoire of the Professional Women's Hockey League (PWHL). Bryan died on July 6, 2022.

Mathias Honsak (born December 20, 1996 in Vienna) is an Austrian football player. He plays as midfielder for 1. FC Heidenheim in the German Bundesliga. Mathieu Carol Garon (born January 9, 1978) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey goaltender. He played parts of 12 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Montreal Canadiens, Los Angeles Kings, Edmonton Oilers, Pittsburgh Penguins, Columbus Blue Jackets, and Tampa Bay Lightning. Outside of the NHL, Garon played for Avangard Omsk of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Before playing in the NHL, Garon played parts of three seasons with the Victoriaville Tigres of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He had a successful time with the Tigres. He was awarded the Jacques Plante Memorial Trophy for being the best goaltender in the QMJHL. He was also named as the CHL Goaltender of the Year and was selected to the QMJHL First All-Star Team and CHL First All-Star team. He was drafted 44th overall by the Montreal Canadiens in the 1996 NHL entry draft. He was immediately sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Fredericton Canadiens and Quebec Citadelles. On October 6, 2000, the Canadiens called him up and Garon made his NHL debut, stopping 18 of 21 shots in an 8–4 loss against the New Jersey Devils. He continued to split his time playing for both the Canadiens and their AHL-affiliates. On August 1, 2001, Garon signed a one-year contract to stay with the Canadiens. On August 2, 2002, Garon signed a one-year contract to stay with the Canadiens and then signed a two-year, $1 million extension on February 28, 2003. On June 26, 2004, the Canadiens traded Garon along with a 2004 third-round draft pick to the Los Angeles Kings in exchange for Radek Bonk and Cristobal Huet. The NHL named Garon as the Defensive Player of the Month for the month of December 2005. On July 17, 2006, Garon signed a one-year contract to stay with the Canadiens. On July 3, 2007, Garon signed a two-year, $2.2 million contract to join the Edmonton Oilers. During his time in Edmonton, Garon split playing time alongside Dwayne Roloson. During his first season with the Oilers, Garon finished with a record with 26—18 record, posting a 2.66 goals against average and a.913 save percentage. On January 29, 2009, the Oilers traded Garon to the Pittsburgh Penguins in exchange for Dany Sabourin, Ryan Stone, and a 2011 fourth-round draft pick. During his time with the Penguins, Garon was the backup goaltender to Marc-André Fleury. He helped the Penguins when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Philadelphia Flyers, Washington Capitals, and Carolina Hurricanes. They went on to defeat the Detroit Red Wings four games to three in the Final to win the first Stanley Cup in Hurricanes franchise history. During Game 5 of the Finals, Fleury let in 5 goals and was pulled in favour of Garon. On July 1, 2009, Garon signed a two-year, $2.4 million contract to join the Columbus Blue Jackets. On January 11, 2010, the NHL named Garon as their Third Star of the Week. On November 8, the NHL named Garon as their Second Star of the Week. On July 1, 2011, Garon signed a two-year, $2.6 million contract to join the Tampa Bay Lightning. He played parts of two seasons with the Lightning. Garon retired from playing professional ice hockey in 2014.

Mathieu Joseph (born February 9, 1997) is a Canadian professional ice hockey winger. He currently plays for the Los Angeles Kings of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Tampa Bay Lightning, Ottawa Senators, and St. Louis Blues. Joseph is a two-time Stanley Cup champion, winning back-to-back championships with the Lighting in 2020 and 2021. Before playing in the NHL, Joseph played four seasons with the Saint John Sea Dogs of the Quebec Major Junior Hockey League (QMJHL). He had a successful time with the Sea Dogs. He was named to the OHL Second All-Star Team and helped the team capture the President's Cup. He was drafted 120th overall by the Tampa Bay Lightning in the 2015 NHL entry draft. On December 24, 2016, Joseph signed a three-year, $2.77 million entry-level contract to join the Lightning. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Syracuse Crunch. On October 6, 2018, the Lightning called him up and Joseph made his NHL debut in a 2–1 shootout win against the Florida Panthers. On October 16, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Tyler Johnson goal in a 4–2 win against the Carolina Hurricanes. On November 4, Joseph scored his first NHL goal against Craig Anderson in a 4–3 overtime win against the Ottawa Senators. He helped the Lightning when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Columbus Blue Jackets, Boston Bruins, and New York Islanders. They went on to defeat the Dallas Stars four games to two in the Final to win the Stanley Cup. On December 23, 2020, Joseph signed a two-year, $1.475 million contract to stay with the Lightning. The Lightning went on to repeat as Stanley Cup champions the next season as well. On March 20, 2022, the Lightning traded Joseph along with a 2024 fourth-round draft pick to the Ottawa Senators in exchange for Nick Paul. On July 28, 2022, Joseph signed a four-year, $11.8 million contract to stay with the Senators. He played parts of three seasons with the Senators. On March 20, 2022, the Senators traded Joseph along with a 2025 third-round draft pick to the St. Louis Blues in exchange for future considerations. He played parts of two seasons with the Blues. On March 6, 2026, Joseph signed a one-year contract to join the Los Angeles Kings.

Mathew Michael Paul Barzal (born May 26, 1997) is a Canadian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the New York Islanders of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was named the Calder Memorial Trophy winner in 2018 and he is a three-time All-Star, being named one in 2019, 2020, and 2024. Before playing in the NHL, Barzal played one season with the Coquitlam Express of the British Columbia Hockey League (BCHL) and four seasons with the Seattle Thunderbirds of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He was drafted 16th overall by the New York Islanders of the 2012 NHL entry draft. On September 10, 2015, Barzal signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Islanders. On October 15, 2016, Barzal made his NHL debut in a 2–1 loss against the Washington Capitals. On October 15, 2017, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Josh Bailey goal in a 5–2 win against the Los Angeles Kings. On October 19, Barzal scored his first NHL goal against Henrik Lundqvist in a 4–3 shootout win against the New York Rangers. On December 23, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 5–2 win against the Winnipeg Jets. On June 20, 2018, Barzal was awarded the Calder Memorial Trophy for being the rookie of the year. On January 11, 2021, Barzal signed a three-year, $21 million contract to stay with the Islanders. On October 4, 2022, Barzal signed a eight-year, $73.2 million contract to stay with the Islanders.

Mathieu David Schneider (born June 12, 1969) is an American former professional ice hockey defenseman. He played parts of 21 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Montreal Canadiens, New York Islanders, Toronto Maple Leafs, New York Rangers, Los Angeles Kings, Detroit Red Wings, Anaheim Ducks, Atlanta Thrashers, Vancouver Canucks, and Phoenix Coyotes. Schneider is a one-time Stanley Cup champion, winning with the Canadiens in 1993. He is also a two-time All-Star, being named one in 1996 and 2003. Before playing in the NHL, Schneider played parts of two seasons with Cornwall Royals of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted 44th overall by the Montreal Canadiens in the 1987 NHL entry draft. He was immediately sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Sherbrooke Canadiens. On October 8, 1987, Montreal called him up and Schneider made his NHL debut in a 2–2 overtime tie against the Philadelphia Flyers. On December 30, 1989, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Mats Näslund goal in a 5–3 loss against the Calgary Flames. On January 7, 1990, Schneider scored his first NHL goal against Kirk McLean in a 5–3 win against the Vancouver Canucks. He helped the Canadiens when they went on a run during the playoffs. They defeated the Quebec Nordiques, Buffalo Sabres, and New York Islanders. They eventually went on to defeat the Los Angeles Kings four games to one in the Finals to win the Stanley Cup. On April 5, 1995, the Canadiens traded Schneider along with Kirk Muller and Craig Darby to the New York Islanders in exchange for Pierre Turgeon and Vladimir Malakhov. During the 1996 season, he was named to his first All-Star Game. On March 13, 1996, the Islanders traded Schneider along with Wendel Clark and D. J. Smith to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for Sean Haggerty, Darby Hendrickson, Kenny Jönsson, and a 1997 first-round pick (#4-Roberto Luongo). It was considered to be one of the most lopsided trades in NHL history. He played parts of three seasons with the Maple Leafs. On October 14, 1998, the Maple Leafs traded Schneider to the New York Rangers in exchange for Alexander Karpovtsev and a 1999 fourth-round pick. The next day, he signed a one-year, $2.75 million contract to stay with the Rangers. On June 23, 2000, Schneider went unprotected in the expansion draft and the Columbus Blue Jackets selected him. He never played a game with the Blue Jackets. On August 13, 2000, Schneider signed a one-year contract to join the Los Angeles Kings. On July 2, 2001, Schneider signed a three-year contract to join the Los Angeles Kings. During the 2002-03 season, he was named to his second All-Star Game. He played parts of three seasons with the Kings. On March 11, 2003, the Kings traded Schneider to the Detroit Red Wings in exchange for Sean Avery, Maxim Kuznetsov a 2003 first round draft pick and a 2004 second-round pick. On August 4, 2005, Schneider signed a two-year contract to stay with the Red Wings. On October 21, Schneider played in his 1,000 NHL game in a 3–2 win against the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim. During the game, he assisted on a Mikael Samuelsson goal. On July 1, 2007, Schneider signed a two-year, $11.25 million contract to join the Anaheim Ducks. He only played one season with the Ducks, scoring 12 goals and recording 27 assists for 39 points. On September 17, 2008, the Ducks placed Schneider on waivers and he cleared them. On September 26, 2008, the Ducks traded Schneider to the Atlanta Thrashers in exchange for Ken Klee, Brad Larsen, and Chad Painchaud. He scored 4 goals and recorded 11 assists for 15 points in 44 games with the Thrashers. On February 16, 2009, the Thrashers traded Schneider along with a 2009 conditional draft pick back to the Montreal Canadiens in exchange for a 2009 second-round draft pick and a 2010 third-round draft pick. In his return to Montreal, he scored 5 goals and recorded 12 assists for 17 points in 23 regular season games. On August 28, 2009, Schneider signed a one-year, $1.55 million contract to join the Vancouver Canucks. During his only season with the Canucks, he scored 2 goals and recorded 3 assists for 5 points in 17 regular season games. On December 29, the Canucks decided to waive Schneider and he cleared them to play for their AHL-affiliate Manitoba Moose. On March 3, 2010, the Canucks traded Schneider to the Phoenix Coyotes in exchange for Sean Zimmerman and a 2010 sixth-round draft pick. Schneider on played 8 games with the team and recorded 4 assists. Schneider decided to retire from playing professional ice hockey at the end of the season and join the National Hockey League Players' Association as a special assistant. Schneider is Jewish and was inducted into the National Jewish Sports Hall of Fame and Museum in 2024.

Matias Maccelli (born October 14, 2000) is a Finnish professional ice hockey winger. He currently plays for the New York Islanders of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Arizona Coyotes, Utah Hockey Club, and Toronto Maple Leafs. Outside of the NHL, Maccelli played for Ilves of the Liiga. Before playing in the NHL, Maccelli played two seasons with the Dubuque Fighting Saints of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and two seasons with Ilves of the Liiga. He had a successful time with his teams. With the Fighting Saints, he was named to the Second All-Star Team. With Ilves, he won the Jarmo Wasama Memorial Trophy for being the rookie of the year. He was drafted 98th overall by the Arizona Coyotes in the 2019 NHL entry draft. On April 29, 2020, Maccelli signed a one-year entry-level contract to join the Coyotes. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Tucson Roadrunners. On 3 March 2022, the Coyotes called him up and Maccelli made his NHL debut in a 2–1 win against the Colorado Avalanche. Two days later on 5 March, Maccelli scored his first NHL goal against Matt Murray in a 8–5 win against the Ottawa Senators. On 17 July 2023, Maccelli signed a two-year, $10.275 million contract to stay with the Coyotes. After the Coyotes franchise was suspended, Maccelli and the rest of the roster were transferred to the new expansion team Utah Hockey Club (now Utah Mammoth). On 30 June 2025, the Mammoth traded Maccelli to the Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for a 2027 conditional third-round draft pick. He scored 14 goals and recorded 24 assists for 39 points in 70 regular season games for the Leafs. On 1 July 2026, Maccelli signed a one-year, $2.25 million contract to join the New York Islanders.

Matjaž Kek (born 9 September 1961) is a Slovenian professional football manager and former player. He is currently the manager of the Slovenia national team. As a player, Kek played over 280 games for Maribor. He also played for Železničar Maribor, as well as for Spittal/Drau and GAK in Austria. He was also capped once by Slovenia, in a friendly against Cyprus in 1992. As a manager, he has coached Maribor, Slovenia, Al-Ittihad, and HNK Rijeka. While with Slovenia, he managed at the 2010 FIFA World Cup and UEFA Euro 2024. Matjaž's father, Franc, played for NK Maribor during the early 1960s. His son, also named Matjaž, is a former footballer. Slovenian PrvaLiga: 1996–97, 1997–98, 1998–99

Mats Johan Sundin (born February 13, 1971) is a Swedish retired professional ice hockey player. Sundin played a career total of 18 seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Quebec Nordiques, Toronto Maple Leafs, and Vancouver Canucks. Sundin served as the team captain of the Toronto Maple Leafs for 11 seasons. When the 2007–08 NHL season ended, Sundin became the longest serving non-North American born captain in NHL history. He last played 41 games with the Vancouver Canucks in the 2008–09 NHL season before he announced his retirement on September 30, 2009. On November 12, 2012, Sundin along with Joe Sakic, Adam Oates, and Pavel Bure was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame.

Mats André Zuccarello Aasen (born 1 September 1987) is a Norwegian professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays for the Minnesota Wild of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the New York Rangers and Dallas Stars. Outside of the NHL, he has played for the Frisk Tigers of the UPC-ligaen/GET-ligaen, Modo Hockey of the Elitserien (SEL), and Metallurg Magnitogorsk of the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). Before playing in the NHL, Zuccarello played parts of five seasons with the Frisk Tigers of the UPC-ligaen/GET-ligaen and thier many juniour teams. He also played two seasons with Modo Hockey of the Elitserien (SEL). He had a successful time with Modo. He led the league with 64 points and was awarded the Guldhjälmen as most valuable player in the Elitserien. He was not drafted by an NHL team. On 26 May 2010, Zuccarello signed a two-year, $900,000 entry-level contract to join the New York Rangers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was immediately sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Hartford Wolf Pack/Connecticut Whale. On 23 December, the Rangers called Zuccarello up and he made his debut in a in a 4–3 shootout loss against the Tampa Bay Lightning. Zuccarello scored during his shot in the shootout. He was sent back down the Whale afterwards. On 27 December, the Rangers called him back up and he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Derek Stepan powerplay goal in a 7–2 win against the New York Islanders. Nine days later, Zuccarello scored his first NHL goal against Cam Ward in a 2–1 overtime win over the Carolina Hurricanes. He scored the overtime-winning goal. On 28 March 2013, Zuccarello signed a one-year contract to return to the Rangers. After the season ended, he signed another one-year, $1.15 million contract to stay with the Rangers. He helped the team during the 2014 Stanley Cup playoffs. They defeated the Philadelphia Flyers, Pittsburgh Penguins, and Montreal Canadiens. They eventually were defeated by the Los Angeles Kings four games to one in the Final. On 22 July 2014, Zuccarello signed a one-year, $3.5 million contract to stay with the Rangers. On 2 March 2015, Zuccarello signed a four-year, $18 million contract extension to stay with the Rangers. On 30 October, Zuccarello recorded his first career NHL hat-trick in a 3–1 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs. During the 2015–16 season, Zuccarello was named as a finalist for the Bill Masterton Memorial Trophy, which was won by Jaromir Jagr of the Florida Panthers. On 4 October 2017, the Rangers named Zuccarello as an alternate captain for the team. On 23 February 2019, the Rangers traded Zuccarello to the Dallas Stars in exchange for a 2019 conditional second-round pick and a 2020 conditional third-round pick. He was only able to play 2 games, scoring 1 goals and recording 2 assists. Most of his tenure with the Stars was spent recovering from injuries he suffered. On 1 July 2019, Zuccarello signed a five-year, $30 million contract to join the Minnesota Wild. On 17 April 2022, Zuccarello recorded both his 51st and 52nd assists which broke the record for most assists in a season by a Wild player. On 29 September 2023, Zuccarello signed a two-year, $8.25 million contract to stay with the Wild.

Sir Alexander Matthew Busby was a Scottish footballer and football manager. He played for Scotland national team. Busby managed Manchester United and led them to great success. Many people believe that Busby is one of the greatest football managers of all time. As a player, Busby played for Manchester City and Liverpool. After his playing career, he went to manage Manchester United and built a great team called the Busby Babes. Eight of those players died in an airplane accident in Munich. This accident was called the Munich air disaster. But Busby again built a winning team after the disaster. He spent 25 years with Manchester United and won 13 trophies. 1Does not include matches for which Jimmy Murphy served as acting manager following the Munich air disaster. Matthew Robert Bonner (born April 5, 1980) is an American professional basketball player with the San Antonio Spurs of the National Basketball Association (NBA). Bonner played college basketball for the University of Florida. He was selected by the Chicago Bulls in the second round of the 2003 NBA Draft. He has also played for the Toronto Raptors. Bonner was named the Verizon Academic All-American of the Year for the sport of basketball in both 2002 and 2003.

Matt Calvert (born December 24, 1989 in Brandon, Manitoba) is a Canadian professional ice hockey player. Drafted in the 5th Round (127th overall) by the Columbus Blue Jackets during the 2008 NHL Entry Draft he currently plays with the Colorado Avalanche. He also played for the Springfield Falcons of the AHL and the Columbus Blue Jackets of the National Hockey League (NHL). He is the only player in WHL history to score three short-handed goals in one period in the playoffs.

Matt Duchene (born January 16, 1991) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre for the Dallas Stars of the National Hockey League (NHL). He also played for the Ottawa Senators, Colorado Avalanche, and Columbus Blue Jackets. He was picked by the Avalanche with the third overall pick in the 2009 NHL Entry Draft. He played in the OHL with the Brampton Battalion. Duchene won the gold medal in the 2008 IIHF World U18 Championships with Canada

Matthew Ellison (born December 8, 1983 in Duncan, British Columbia) is a Canadian professional ice hockey right winger. He currently plays in the Kontinental Hockey League for Torpedo Nizhny Novgorod. He was picked by the Chicago Blackhawks with the one hundred and twenty-eighth overall pick in the 2002 NHL Entry Draft. e played in the NHL for the Chicago Blackhawks before being traded to the Philadelphia Flyers along with a 3rd-round pick in the 2006 NHL Entry Draft for Patrick Sharp and Éric Meloche. He signed a one-year contract on July 4, 2008 to play in Latvia with the Dinamo Riga of the Kontinental Hockey League before signing with HC MVD.

Matthew Paul Clement (born August 12, 1974, in Butler, Pennsylvania) is a former Major League Baseball starting pitcher. Clement played for the San Diego Padres, Florida Marlins, Chicago Cubs and Boston Red Sox. While on the Red Sox active roster, he was injured all of the 2007 season. He batted and threw right-handed. On April 5, 2009, Clement said he was no longer going to play baseball.

Matthew David Cooke (born September 7, 1978) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey left winger. He played parts of seventeen seasons in the National Hockey League (NHL). He played for the Vancouver Canucks, Washington Capitals, Pittsburgh Penguins, and Minnesota Wild. During his career, he was known as a pest because of his way of aggravating opponents. He also faced many suspensions by the NHL. In 2009, he won the Stanley Cup with the Pittsburgh Penguins. He won a gold medal with Team Canada in the 2010 World Ice Hockey Championships. He won the Stanley Cup in 2009. (Pittsburgh Penguins)

Matthew Daniel "Matt" Batts (October 16, 1921 – July 14, 2013) was a Major League Baseball catcher. He played from 1947 through 1956 for the Boston Red Sox (1947–1951), St. Louis Browns (1951), Detroit Tigers (1952–1954), Chicago White Sox (1954) and Cincinnati Reds (1955–1956). Batts was born on October 16, 1921 in San Antonio, Texas. He died on July 14, 2013 in Baton Rouge, Louisiana from natural causes, aged 91.

Matthew Jason Bloom (born November 14, 1972) is an American former professional wrestler and professional football player. He works for the WWE. Bloom is the head trainer at the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Florida. Bloom is best known for his work with WWE as Prince Albert, Albert and A-Train from 1999 to 2004, and as Lord Tensai and Tensai from 2012 to 2014. He also wrestled in Japan from 2005 to 2012 with All Japan Pro Wrestling (AJPW), New Japan Pro-Wrestling (NJPW) and Pro Wrestling Noah (Noah) as Giant Bernard. During his career, Bloom has held the GHC Tag Team Championship, IWGP Tag Team Championship and WWF Intercontinental Championship. IWGP Tag Team Championship (two times) (with Travis Tomko (one) and Karl Anderson (one)) G1 Tag League (2009) (with Karl Anderson) He was ranked #45 of the top 500 singles wrestlers in the PWI 500 in 2012. GHC Tag Team Championship (one time) (with Karl Anderson) WWF Intercontinental Championship (one time) Tag Team of the Year (2011) (with Karl Anderson) 1After he won the championship, he held it by himself.

Matthew Martin Carpenter (born November 26, 1985) is a professional baseball player. He plays for the St. Louis Cardinals. The positions he plays are second and third base. Carpenter played his major league game on June 4, 2011 at Busch Stadium. He became their regular leadoff hitter early in the 2013 season.

Matthew Carle (born September 25, 1984) is an American professional ice hockey defenseman. He currently plays for the Tampa Bay Lightning of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the San Jose Sharks and Philadelphia Flyers. Before playing in the NHL, Carle played parts of 2 seasons with the US National Team Development Program, 1 season with the River City Lancers of the United States Hockey League (USHL), and 3 years of college hockey with the University of Denver Pioneers. During his time with the Pioneers, Carle won the Hobey Baker Award in 2006 for being the top National Collegiate Athletic Association men's ice hockey player. He was also the only junior defenseman in history to win the award. He was drafted 47th overall by the San Jose Sharks in the 2003 NHL Entry Draft. On March 25, 2006, Carle made his NHL debut and scored his first NHL goal against Manny Fernandez of the Minnesota Wild in a 5-1 win. On November 21, 2007, Carle was signed to a four-year, $13.75 million contract extension to stay with San Jose. On July 4, 2008, the Sharks traded Carle along with Ty Wishart and a first round pick in the 2009 NHL Entry Draft and a fourth round pick in 2010, to the Tampa Bay Lightning in exchange for Dan Boyle and Brad Lukowich. After 12 games with the Lightning, they traded him along with a 2009 third round draft pick to the Philadelphia Flyers in exchange for Steve Eminger, Steve Downie and a 2009 fourth round pick on November 7, 2008. Carle missed 5 games at the start of December because of a rib injury. During the home opener of the 2009–10 season for the Flyers, Carle tied the NHL record for assists in a single period by a defenceman when he set up four goals in the second period against the Washington Capitals and also helped Mike Richards achieve his second career hat trick, which was also his personal best for assists in a game. On July 4, 2012, Carle signed a six-year; $33 million contract to return with the Tampa Bay Lightning.

Matthew John Anderson (born April 18, 1987) is an American volleyball player. He is a member of the United States men's national volleyball team and the Russian club Zenit Kazan. He played volleyball at the Olympic Games in London in 2012. He was a NORCECA Champion 2013. He won gold medals at the 2008 Pan American Cup, 2014 World League and 2015 World Cup.

Matthew Lee Cappotelli (November 12, 1979 – June 29, 2018) was an American professional wrestler. He was born in Caledonia, New York. He won the Tough Enough III with John Hennigan. He worked in Ohio Valley Wrestling (OVW), the primary developmental territory for WWE. In July 2017, Cappotelli was diagnosed with glioblastoma, a rare form of brain cancer. He stopped his cancer treatment in May 2018. He died on June 29, 2018 in Louisville, Kentucky, aged 38.

Matthew Albert Blair (September 20, 1950 – October 22, 2020) was an American football player. He was an outside linebacker for the Minnesota Vikings of the National Football League (NFL) for all 12 seasons of his career from 1974 to 1985. Blair was born in Hilo, Hawaii. Blair died on October 22, 2020 from problems caused by chronic traumatic encephalopathy in Minneapolis, Minnesota at the age of 70.

Matthew James Doherty (born 16 January 1992) is an Irish professional footballer who plays for Premier League club Wolverhampton Wanderers and the Republic of Ireland national team. Scores and results list the Republic of Ireland's goal tally first. Wolverhampton Wanderers Player of the Year: 2015–16 Professional Footballers' Association Fans' Premier League Player of the Month: September 2018

Matthew Coronato (born November 14, 2002) is an American professional ice hockey winger. He currently plays for the Calgary Flames of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Coronato played two seasons with the Chicago Steel of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and two years with the Harvard Crimson of ECAC Hockey (ECAC). He had a successful time with his teams. With the Steel, he was named the USHL Forward of the Year and was also named to both the All-Rookie Second Team and All-USHL First Team. The 2020–21 season was very successful for the team, finishing with a record of 38–11–3 and being awarded the Anderson Cup as regular season champions. He helped the Steel when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Dubuque Fighting Saints and Muskegon Lumberjacks in the opening rounds. They went on to defeat the Fargo Force three games to one in the Final to win the Clark Cup. With the Crimson, he was named a AHCA East Second Team All-American and was also named to both the ECAC All-Rookie Team and All-ECAC Second Team. He was drafted 13th overall by the Calgary Flames in the 2021 NHL entry draft. On March 15, 2022, Coronato signed a three-year, $925,000 entry-level contract to join the Flames. On December 13, 2025, Coronato made his NHL debut in a 3–1 win against the San Jose Sharks. On April 20, Coronato scored his first NHL goal against Alex Nedeljkovic on the power play in a 5–2 loss against the Pittsburgh Penguins. The next season, he was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Calgary Wranglers before being called back up after the season. On May 3, 2025, Coronato signed a seven-year, $45.5 million contract to stay with the Flames.

Matthew Grzelcyk (born January 5, 1994) is an American professional ice hockey defenseman. He currently plays for the Chicago Blackhawks of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Boston Bruins and Pittsburgh Penguins. Before playing in the NHL, Grzelcyk played four years with the Boston University Terriers of Hockey East. He served as the captain of the Terriers. He helped the Terriers when they went on a run in the Beanpot tournament. They made it to the finals where they defeated the Northeastern Huskies in a 6–2 overtime win. Grzelcyk scored the overtime winning goal and was named the MVP of the tournament. He was drafted 85th overall by the Boston Bruins in the 2012 NHL entry draft. On April 1, 2016, he signed a two-year entry-level contract to join the Bruins. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Providence Bruins. On December 14, 2016, the Bruins called him up and Grzelcyk made his NHL debut in a 4–3 overtime loss against the Pittsburgh Penguins. On November 22, 2017, he recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Jake DeBrusk goal in a 3–2 shootout win against the New Jersey Devils. On November 24, Grzelcyk scored his first NHL goal against Matt Murray in a 4–3 win against the Pittsburgh Penguins. On June 15, 2018, Grzelcyk signed a two-year, $2.8 million contract to stay with the Bruins. On July 1, 2024, Grzelcyk signed a one-year, $2.75 million to join the Pittsburgh Penguins. During hiss season with the Penguins, he scored 1 goal and recorded 39 assists for 40 points. On October 5, 2025, Grzelcyk signed a one-year, $1 million to join the Chicago Blackhawks.

Matthew Benning (born May 25, 1994) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He is currently is an unrestricted free agent. He has played for the Edmonton Oilers, Nashville Predators, San Jose Sharks, and Toronto Maple Leafs of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Benning played two seasons with the Spruce Grove Saints of the Alberta Junior Hockey League (AJHL), one season with the Dubuque Fighting Saints of the United States Hockey League (USHL), and three years with the Northeastern Huskies of Hockey East. He was drafted 175th overall by the Boston Bruins of the 2012 NHL entry draft. He never played a game for the Bruins. On August 27, 2016, Benning signed a three-year, $2.15 million entry-level contract to join the Edmonton Oilers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Bakersfield Condors. On November 1, 2016, the Oilers called him up and Benning made his NHL debut in a 3–2 overtime loss against the Toronto Maple Leafs. On November 5, he recorded his first two NHL points after assisting on a goals by Patrick Maroon and Leon Draisaitl in a 3–2 shootout win against the New York Islanders. On January 7, 2017, Benning scored his first NHL goal against Cory Schneider in a 2–1 overtime win against the New Jersey Devils. On October 9, 2020, Benning signed a two-year, $2 million contract to join the Nashville Predators. He played two season with the Predators. On July 13, 2022, Benning signed a four-year, $5 million contract to join the San Jose Sharks. He was forced to end his season after he suffered a hip injury and needed surgery. He played three seasons with the Sharks. On October 30, 2024, the Sharks traded Benning along with a 2025 conditional third-round draft pick and a 2026 sixth-round draft pick to he Toronto Maple Leafs in exchange for Timothy Liljegren. He played one regular season game with the Leafs. Benning comes from a hockey family. His father Brian, uncle Jim, and younger brother Michael are all involved in professional hockey.

Matthew Edward Boldy (born April 5, 2001) is an American professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Vegas Golden Knights of the National Hockey League (NHL). Internationally, Boldy plays for the United States, winning a gold medal in 2026. Before playing in the NHL, Boldy played two seasons with the U.S. National Development Team of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and two years with the Boston College Eagles of Hockey East. He had a successful time with his teams. With the Eagles, he was named to both the Hockey East All-Rookie Team and All-Hockey East First Team. He was also named an AHCA East First Team All-American. He was drafted 12th overall by the Minnesota Wild of the 2019 NHL entry draft. On March 31, 2021, Boldy signed an three-year entry-level contract to join the Wild. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliates Iowa Wild. On January 6, 2022, Minnesota called him up and Boldy made his NHL debut in a 3–2 win against the Boston Bruins. During the second period, he scored his first NHL goal against Jeremy Swayman. On February 14, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 7–4 win against the Detroit Red Wings. On January 16, 2023, Boldy signed a seven-year, $49 million contract to stay with the Leafs.

Matthew Moore Hardy (born September 23, 1974) is an American professional wrestler. He is currently signed to Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA), where he is one-half of the TNA World Tag Team Champions in his fourth reign. He is also known for his time in the World Wrestling Federation/WWE and All Elite Wrestling (AEW). With his brother, Jeff Hardy, he became one of the most famous tag team wrestlers. Between WWE, TNA and Ring of Honor, Hardy is a 16-time world tag team champion and a three-time world champion as a singles star (with one reign as ECW Champion, and two as TNA World Heavyweight Champion). Matthew R. Joyce (born August 3, 1984) is an outfielder for the Oakland Athletics. He has also played for the Detroit Tigers, Tampa Bay Rays, Los Angeles Angels of Anaheim, and Pittsburgh Pirates. In 2011, Joyce was picked to play in the Major League Baseball All-Star Game.

Matthew Rhys Holland (born 11 April 1974) is a former Irish-British footballer. He played as a midfielder. Football League First Division play-offs: 2000 AFC Bournemouth Player of the Year: 1995–96 Ipswich Town Player of the Year: 1997–98, 2002–03 Charlton Athletic Player of the Year: 2007–08

Matthew Allen Hughes (born December 13, 1978 in Hillsboro, Illinois) is a retired American mixed martial artist. Hughes is a former two-time UFC Welterweight Champion and UFC Hall of Famer. He put together two separate six-fight winning streaks. He defeated all the available opposition in his weight class. He defeated six former UFC Champions. Hughes also was the coach for the reality shows The Ultimate Fighter 2 and The Ultimate Fighter 6. He was the host of Trophy Hunters TV. On June 16, 2017, Hughes was hospitalized with a serious head injury after a train struck the passenger side of his truck at a crossing near his home in Montgomery County, Illinois. Matt Harvey (born March 27, 1989) is an American professional baseball player. He is a pitcher for the New York Mets. He joined the Mets in 2010 after he finished school. Harvey spent two years pitching in the minor leagues before going to the Mets in July 2012. In his first year, he had 3 wins and 5 losses with a 2.75 ERA. In the 2013 season, his pitching improved. He was the starting pitcher in the all star game at Citi Field, his home stadium. In August 2013, Harvey's arm was injured. The injury caused him to miss all of 2014. He returned to play in 2015. Due to a planned surgery he will not play the 2017 season.

Matthew Ryan "Matt" Kemp (born September 23, 1984) is a former American professional baseball player. He is currently a special advisor for the Dodgers. He played the position of outfielder. He has previously played for the Los Angeles Dodgers and the San Diego Padres. His career began in 2006. Kemp was drafted by the Dodgers in the sixth round of the 2003 draft. He went to the major leagues after four years in the minor leagues. He did not become a full-time player until 2008. He became the everyday starting center fielder. He has been named to two All-Star teams. He has won two Gold Glove Awards. He has won two Silver Slugger Awards.

Matthew Edward "Matt" Hobden (27 March 1993 – 2 January 2016) was an English cricketer. He was a right-handed batsman and a right-arm fast-medium bowler. He played for Cardiff MCCU (2012–2013) and Sussex (2013–2016). Hobden was born in Eastbourne, East Sussex. He was educated at Millfield School and Eastbourne College. Hobden died after accidentally falling on 2 January 2016 in Forres, Scotland. He was 22.

Matt Nagy (born April 24, 1978) is an American football coach and former quarterback. He is the head coach of the Chicago Bears of the National Football League (NFL) since 2018. He was born in Dunellen, New Jersey. He played for the New York Dragons, Carolina Cobras, Georgia Force, Columbus Destroyers and the Philadelphia Eagles.

Matthew Lon Keough (July 3, 1955 – May 1, 2020) was an American professional baseball player. He was born in Pomona, California. He played in Major League Baseball (MLB) as a right-handed pitcher for the Oakland Athletics (1977–1983), New York Yankees (1983–1984), St. Louis Cardinals (1985), Chicago Cubs (1986) and Houston Astros (1986). From 1987 to 1990, he played for the Japanese baseball team Hanshin Tigers. Keough died on May 1, 2020 at the age of 64.

Matt Beresford Poore (June 1, 1930 – June 11, 2020) was an international New Zealand cricketer. He played 14 Tests for New Zealand in the 1950s. He was born in Christchurch. Poore died at a retirement home in North Shore Auckland, on 11 June 2020 at the age of 90.

Matt LaFleur (born November 3, 1979) is an American football coach who is the head coach of the Green Bay Packers of the National Football League (NFL). LaFleur became the Packers’ head coach in 2019 and has led the team to multiple playoff appearances and division titles. LaFleur was born in Mount Pleasant, Michigan and attended Saginaw Valley State University, where he played quarterback for the Cardinals. After college, he began his coaching career as a graduate assistant and offensive assistant at various collegiate programs. LaFleur spent several years coaching in the college football ranks and the NFL as an assistant. He held positions with the Oakland Raiders, Washington Redskins, Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams, and Tennessee Titans as a quarterbacks coach or offensive coordinator before being hired as a head coach. LaFleur was hired as the Packers’ head coach on January 8, 2019. In his first season, he guided the team to a 13–3 record, winning the NFC North division and earning a first-round bye in the playoffs. LaFleur was named NFC Coach of the Year for his success. Under his leadership, the Packers have consistently competed for playoff berths and have maintained one of the league’s most potent offenses. He works closely with quarterback Aaron Rodgers and has emphasized an aggressive, pass-oriented offensive strategy. LaFleur is married and has children. He is known for his family-oriented approach and involvement in community programs through the Packers organization.

Matthew Murray (born May 25, 1994) is a Canadian professional ice hockey goaltender. He currently plays for the Seattle Kraken of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Pittsburgh Penguins, Ottawa Senators, and Toronto Maple Leafs. Murray is a two-time Stanley Cup champion, winning back-to-back cups with the Penguins in 2016 and 2017. Before playing in the NHL, Murray played four seasons with the Sault Ste. Marie Greyhounds of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He had a successful time with his teams. He was named to the Second All-Star Team. He was drafted 83rd overall by the Pittsburgh Penguins in the 2012 NHL entry draft. On September 4, 2013, Murray signed a two-year, $1.95 million entry-level contract to join the Penguins. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins. On December 19, 2015, Pittsburgh called him up and Murray made his NHL debut, stopping 24 of 26 shots in a 2–1 loss against the Carolina Hurricanes. Two days later, he earned his first NHL career win in a 5–2 win against the Columbus Blue Jackets. On April 2, 2016, Murray stopped all 24 shots he first to earn his first NHL career shutout in a 5–2 win against the New York Islanders. He helped the Penguins when they went on a run in the playoffs, serving as the backup goaltender for Marc-André Fleury. They defeated the New York Rangers, Washington Capitals, and Tampa Bay Lightning. They went on to defeat the San Jose Sharks four games to two in the Final to win the Stanley Cup. On October 20, Murray signed a three-year, $3.75 million contract to stay with the Penguins. He battled Fleury for starting position during the playoffs the next season. The Penguins went on to win their second straight Stanley Cup, defeatin the Nashville Predators four games to two in the Final. On October 7, 2020, the Penguins traded Murray to the Ottawa Senators in exchange for Jonathan Gruden and a 2020 second-round draft pick. On October 9, Murray signed a four-year, $25 million contract to stay with the Senators. On November 28, 2021, the Senators decided to place Murray onto waivers and he was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Belleville Senators. On July 11, 2022, the Senators traded Murray along with a 2023 third-round draft pick, and a 2024 seventh-round draft pick to the Toronto Maple Leafs for future considerations. He played 26 regular season games before being sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Toronto Marlies. On July 2, 2024, Murray signed a one-year contract to stay with the Leafs. On July 1, 2025, Murray signed a one-year, $1 million contract to join the Seattle Kraken.

Matt Luff (born May 5, 1997) is a Canadian professional ice hockey winger. He currently plays for the Hamilton Hammers of the American Hockey League (AHL) and is a prospect with the New York Islanders of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Los Angeles Kings, Nashville Predators, Detroit Red Wings, and St. Louis Blues. Before playing in the NHL, Luff played one season with the Belleville Bulls and two seasons with the Hamilton Bulldogs of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was not drafted by an NHL team. On September 23, 2016, Luff signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Los Angeles Kings of the National Hockey League (NHL). He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Ontario Reign. On November 3, 2018, the Kings called him up and Luff made his NHL debut in a 4–1 win against the Columbus Blue Jackets. On November 19, Luff scored his first NHL goal against Jake Allen in a 2–0 win against the St. Louis Blues. On July 28, 2021, Luff signed a one-year contract to join the Nashville Predators. He scored 3 goals and recorded 3 assists for 6 points in 23 regular season games for the Predators. On July 28, 2021, Luff signed a one-year contract to join the Detroit Red Wings. On July 1, 2023, Luff signed a one-year contract to stay with the Red Wings. He scored 2 goals and recorded 2 assists for 4 points in 19 regular season games for the Red Wings. On July 1, 2025, Luff signed a one-year contract to join the St. Louis Blues. He played 5 regular season games with the Blues and scored 1 goal. He mainly spent his time with their AHL-affiliate Springfield Thunderbirds. On February 24, 2026, the Blues traded Luff to the New York Islanders in exchange for Julien Gauthier.

Matthew Kiersted (born April 14, 1998) is an American professional ice hockey defenseman. He currently plays for the Minnesota Wild of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Florida Panthers. Before playing in the NHL, Kiersted played three seasons with the Chicago Steel of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and four years with the North Dakota Fighting Hawks of the National Collegiate Hockey Conference (NCHC). He had a successful time with his teams. He helped the Steel when they went on a run in the playoffs. They defeated the Youngstown Phantoms and Dubuque Fighting Saints in the opening rounds. They went on to defeat the Sioux City Musketeers three games to two in the Final to win the Clark Cup. With the Fighting Hawks, he was named to the NCHC Second All-Star Team and NCHC First All-Star Team. He was also named a AHCA West Second Team All-American. He was not drafted by an NHL team. On April 1, 2021, Kiersted signed an two-year entry-level contract to join the Florida Panthers of the National Hockey League (NHL). On April 3, 2021, Kiersted made his NHL debut in a 5–2 win against the Columbus Blue Jackets. On October 16, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Sam Bennett goal in a 5–1 win against the New York Islanders. On December 16, Kiersted scored his first NHL goal against Jonathan Quick in a 4–1 loss against the Los Angeles Kings. On June 27, 2022, Kiersted signed a two-year contract to stay with the Panthers. On June 28, 2024, Kiersted signed a one-year contract to stay with the Panthers. On July 2, 2025, Kiersted signed a two-year contract to join the Minnesota Wild.

Matthew Robert Kaye (born June 26, 1974) is an American professional wrestler and commentator. He is best known for working for the WWE from 2005 to 2013 under the ring name, Matt Striker. He currently works as a commentator for Championship Wrestling from Hollywood. He has also won a Slammy Award in 2008 for Announce Team of the Year which he shared with Todd Grisham. On June 20, 2013, he left the WWE when the company did not renew his contract.

Matthew Robert Smith (born 28 October 1982) is an English actor. He is best known as the eleventh form of the Doctor on the British television series Doctor Who. He received a BAFTA Award nomination for the role in 2011. He wanted to be a professional footballer. A back injury made him stop playing the sport. He joined the National Youth Theatre and studied Drama and Creative Writing at the University of East Anglia. Smith became an actor in 2003. He performed in plays like Murder in the Cathedral, Fresh Kills, The History Boys and On the Shore of the Wide World in London theatres. On West End, he has performed in Swimming with Sharks with Christian Slater, and That Face. Smith's first television role was in 2006. He portrayed Jim Taylor in the BBC version of Philip Pullman's The Ruby in the Smoke and The Shadow in the North. His first major role in television came as Danny in the 2007 BBC series Party Animals. Smith is the youngest person to play the character in the British television series. Smith was born on 28 October 1982 in Northampton, England. He attended Northampton School for Boys. He planned to be a professional football player. Smith had played for the youth teams of Northampton Town F.C., Nottingham Forest F.C. and Leicester City F.C. After an injury, he began to study acting. After school, Smith studied Drama and Creative Writing at the University of East Anglia. While acting in On the Shore of the Wide World, the play moved to the Royal National Theatre in London. After finishing, he took on the role of Lockwood in the Alan Bennett play The History Boys. After The History Boys, he acted in Burn/Chatroom/Citizenship and Swimming with Sharks. ""Swimming with Sharks was his first West End play. His first television role was as Jim Taylor in the BBC version of the Sally Lockhart series of books The Ruby in the Smoke and The Shadow in the North. He acted along with Billie Piper in the series. He acted with Piper a third time in an episode of Secret Diary of a Call Girl. Piper is well known for playing the part of Rose Tyler on Doctor Who. Smith was revealed as the Eleventh Doctor in the British science-fiction television series Doctor Who in January 2009 to replace David Tennant, who announced that he left in October 2008. Smith was not as well known as many of the actors who were thought to be likely to get the part. These included Paterson Joseph, David Morrissey, Sean Pertwee, James Nesbitt, Russell Tovey, Catherine Zeta Jones, Chiwetel Ejiofor, Robert Carlyle and Billie Piper. Smith was one of the first actors to audition for the role. Producer Steven Moffat and BBC Wales Head of Drama and executive producer, Piers Wenger immediately liked him for the part. Smith had auditioned for the role of John Watson in the Moffat-created Sherlock at the same time. He did not get the part of Watson because Moffat believed his acting style was closer to Sherlock Holmes but they had already cast Benedict Cumberbatch as Holmes. At 26 years old, Smith was three years younger than Peter Davison was at the time of his casting as the Doctor in 1981. He was younger than any other actor suggested for the role. After three weeks of auditions, Moffat and Wenger agreed that it had "always been Matt". The BBC were was not certain that a 26-year-old could not play the Doctor correctly. Some fans of the show believed that Smith was too young for the role. Others supported him based on what he had shows of his acting ability. For his work in his first series he was nominated in the "Outstanding Drama Performance Category" of the National Television Awards. In June 2010, he appeared on stage with Orbital. They performed a version of the Doctor Who theme at the Glastonbury Festival. Smith hosted the Doctor Who Prom at the Royal Albert Hall on 24–25 July 2010. In June 2011, the BBC said that Smith had been signed to do fourteen more episodes of Doctor Who as the Doctor.

Matthew Stajan (; born December 19, 1983) is a Canadian former professional ice hockey centre. Before playing in the NHL, Stajan played three seasons with the Belleville Bulls of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted with the 57th overall pick by the Toronto Maple Leafs in the 2002 NHL Entry Draft. On January 31, 2010, the Maple Leafs traded Stajan along with Niklas Hagman, Ian White and Jamal Mayers in exchange for Dion Phaneuf, Fredrik Sjöström and Keith Aulie. He is married to his wife Katie and they live in Calgary. Their first child named Emerson, died on March 3, 2014 shortly after birth.

Matthew Joseph Korklan (born March 19, 1983), is an American professional wrestler. He is currently signed to All Elite Wrestling (AEW) and wrestles under the name Matt Sydal. He is also known for his time working with WWE where he competed under the ring name Evan Bourne from 2008 to 2014. He also wrestled for Total Nonstop Action Wrestling/Impact Wrestling, Ring of Honor (ROH), and New Japan Pro-Wrestling (NJPW). He held many titles during his career, including the WWE Tag Team Championship with Kofi Kingston, the Impact Grand Championship, and the Impact X Division Championship. Matt Schaub (born June 25, 1981) is an American football player. He plays quarterback for the Houston Texans of the NFL. He played college football for the Virginia Caveliers. Schaub was drafted by the Atlanta Falcons in 2004. He played with the Falcons for three years behind Michael Vick. Schaub signed with the Texans in 2007. He became a solid starter and was selected to the 2009 Pro Bowl. In 2011, Schaub had a season-ending injury. Schaub was replaced by rookie TJ. Yates and veteran Jake Delhomme.

Matt Vasgersian (born September 28, 1967) is an American sportscaster. He works for MLB Network. He is the new pregame/postgame show host for MLB on Foxreplacing Chris Rose in the MLB Network studios. He does occasional play-by-play for Fox Saturday Baseball. He is also the lead play-by-play for Thursday Night Baseball for MLB Network. He also called baseball games for the San Diego Padres, Milwaukee Brewers, MLB on TBS, Tucson Toros, High Desert Mavericks, and baseball & softball at the 2004 Summer Olympics on NBC. His trademark was: Santa Maria! on a walk off hit, a great play, a no hitter, or a perfect game. He is also the host of Baseball IQ, MLB Network's first ever game show. He has also hosted other shows for Fox Sports Net such as Celebrity Blackjack, Sports Geniuses, Poker Superstars Invitational Tournament, National Heads-Up Poker Championship, and the International World Championships of Rock Paper Scissors. In addition to baseball, poker, and game shows, he has called Olympic games and football. Vasgersian was the announcer for ski jumping at the 2006 Winter Olympics for NBC and anchored the 2008 Summer Olympics and 2010 Winter Olympics for the NBC family. Vasgersian called one season for NBC's coverage of the XFL before it folded. He also called BCS games for Fox most notably with Terry Donahue and Pat Haden and sideline reporter Laura Okmin. Vasgersian also called NFL games for Fox from 2005 until 2009 when MLB Network launched. However, he returned for Week 17 of the 2009 NFL season. Vasgersian also called USC Trojans men's basketball for Fox Sports Net and has been a fill-in voice for UFC on FSN when Mike Goldberg was studio hosting for college football.

Matthew Joseph Underhill (born September 16, 1979 in Campbell River, British Columbia) is a Canadian retired ice hockey goaltender. Before playing hockey professionally, Underhill played in college for Cornell University for 4 years. He was drafted with the 170th overall pick in the 1999 NHL draft by the Calgary Flames. Even though he was drafted by the Flames, he did not play a game for them. The only game the Underhill played in the NHL was during the 2003–04 NHL season for the Chicago Blackhawks. He spent most of his playing career in the AHL and ECHL. He won the ECAC’s Ken Dryden Award in 2002. He played 18 games in the AHL for the Providence Bruins, Manchester Monarchs, Norfolk Admirals and St. John's Maple Leafs. In the ECHL, he played 4 seasons with the Pee Dee Pride, Florence Pride, Mississippi Sea Wolves and Alaska Aces. He retired in 2006 after his season with the Aces. He was inducted into the Cornell Athletic Hall of Fame on November 3rd, 2012.

Matthew Wade Stairs (born February 27, 1968) is a Canadian former professional baseball outfielder, first baseman, and designated hitter, who holds the record for most pinch-hit home runs in Major League Baseball (MLB) history with 23. His pinch-hit home run in the eighth inning of Game 4 in the 2008 National League Championship Series off the Los Angeles Dodgers reliever Jonathan Broxton was called one of the most memorable home runs in Phillies history. In his career, Stairs played for more teams than any position player in MLB history (12 — technically 13 teams, but 12 franchises, as he played for the Montreal Expos and Washington Nationals); Edwin Jackson holds the record for pitchers and all players at 14. He was the second Canadian-born player ever to hit more than thirty-five home runs in a season, and only the second to hit more than 25 home runs and drive in more than 100 runs in back-to-back seasons. He ranks either first or second in power hitting categories for Canadian major leaguers. Stairs also holds the all-time MLB record of home runs hit as a pinch-hitter with 23. His ability to pinch hit made him a valuable asset to several teams and earned him the nickname "Matt Stairs – Professional Hitter". Stairs, Larry Walker, Justin Morneau, Jason Bay, and Joey Votto are the only Canadian MLB players to hit at least 200 career home runs. On February 4, 2015, Stairs was elected to the Canadian Baseball Hall of Fame.

Matthew Tees (13 October 1939 – 4 November 2020) was a Scottish footballer. He played for Grimsby Town (two spells), Charlton Athletic and Luton Town before ending his career with Boston United in the Northern Premier League. He died on 4 November 2020.

Matthew Marinelli (born March 20, 1985) is an American professional wrestler. He currently wrestles for All Elite Wrestling (AEW) and their sister promotion Ring of Honor (ROH) under the ring name Matt Taven. He is a member of The Undisputed Kingdom stable. Taven has also made appearances in Ring of Honor (ROH) (before AEW's buyout), New Japan Pro-Wrestling (NJPW), Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (CMLL), and Impact Wrestling. Taven has won many championships over the course of his career. In CMLL, Taven was a one-time NWA World Historic Welterweight Champion. In Impact, he was a one-time Impact World Tag Team Champion. In NJPW, he was a one-time IWGP Tag Team Champion. In ROH, he is a one-time ROH World Champion, one-time ROH World Television Champion, three-time ROH World Tag Team Champion, three time and first ROH World Six-Man Tag Team Champion, the winner of the Top Prospect Tournament in 2013 and ROH World Six-Man Tag Team Championship Tournament in 2016, and is a Fifth Triple Crown Champion, as well as a Second Grand Slam Champion. On the October 14, 2022 episode of Rampage, Taven made his AEW alongside Mike Bennett and Maria Kanellis. On the October 28 episode of Rampage, Taven challenged Wardlow for his AEW TNT Championship but was unsuccessful. At Supercard of Honor, Taven and Bennett entered the "Reach for the Sky" ladder match in an attempt to win the vacant ROH World Tag Team Championships but the match was won by The Lucha Brothers (Penta El Zero Miedo and Rey Fénix). At Death Before Dishonor, Taven and Bennett challenged for the ROH World Tag Team Championship in a four-way tag team match but it was won by Aussie Open (Kyle Fletcher and Mark Davis). In December 2023, Taven and Bennett wore masks and were called "The Devil's Masked Men". At New Year's Smash, they both defeated MJF in a handicap match to win the ROH World Tag Team Championship. At Worlds End, Taven and Bennett were revealed as the masked men and they created the Undisputed Kingdom stable, alongside Adam Cole, Roderick Strong, and Wardlow. At Battle of the Belts XI, The Undisputed Kingdom challenged The Sons of Texas (Dustin Rhodes, Marshall Von Erich, and Ross Von Erich) for the vacant ROH World Six-Man Tag Team Championships but were unsuccessful. On the August 17 episode of Collision, The Undisputed Kingdom lost the ROH World Tag Team Championships to Dustin Rhodes and Sammy Guevara. On the September 21 episode of Collision, Taven and Bennett challenged Sons of Texas to a rematch for the ROH World Tag Team Title in a Bunkhouse Brawl but lost. On the October 3 episode of ROH on HonorClub, Taven challenged Mark Briscoe for his ROH World Championship but was unsuccessful.

Matthew Rempe (born June 29, 2002) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the New York Rangers of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Rempe played parts of three seasons with the Seattle Thunderbirds of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He was drafted 165th overall by the New York Rangers in the 2020 NHL entry draft. On November 3, 2021, he signed a three-year, entry-level contract to join the Rangers. He was immediately sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Hartford Wolf Pack. On February 18, 2024, the Rangers called him up and he made his NHL debut during the 2024 NHL Stadium Series in a 6–5 overtime win against the New York Islanders. He became the first NHL player to make their debut during a game outdoors. On February 22, the NHL suspended Rempe after he illegally hit New Jersey Devils player Nathan Bastian in the head. On February 24, Rempe scored his first NHL goal against Samuel Ersson in a 4–2 loss against the Philadelphia Flyers. Rempe was suspended for four games after he elbowed Devils' player Jonas Siegenthaler in the head on March 11. On June 18, 2025, Rempe signed a two-year, $1.95 million to stay with the Rangers.
Matthew Bingley (born 16 August 1971) is a former Australian football player. He has played for Australia national team. FIFA Confederations Cup: 1997 (Runners-up)

Matteo Elias Kenzo Guendouzi Valverde Mendoza Olié (; born 14 April 1999) is a French footballer. He plays as a midfielder for Ligue 1 club Marseille and the France national team.

Matteo Schablas (14 March 2005 in Aichach, Germany) is a Austrian professional footballer who plays as a left-back for Austrian Bundesliga club Austria Wien. Schablas began his career at TSV Inchenhofen. He moved to FC Augsburg for the 2014/15 season. For the 2015/16 season he went to the youth team of FC Bayern Munich. From the 2021/22 season he was part of the squad for the U-19 team, for which he also played in the UEFA Youth League in the 2022/23 season. For the 2023/24 season, Schablas moved to the Austrian second division club FC Liefering. He made his debut in the second division 0 28 July 2023 when he came on as a substitute for Moussa Kounfolo Yeo in the 80th minute against FC Dornbirn 1913 on the first day of that season. Schablas joined Austrian Bundesliga club Austria Wien on 31 January 2025. Schablas made his debut for the Austrian U-18 team against Sweden in September 2022.

Matteo Pessina (born 21 April 1997) is an Italian professional footballer who plays as a Midfielder for Monza in the Serie A and Italy National football Team. He joined Monza in 2013 and He beat Pordenone 6-3 In 30 May 2015. On 30 June 2015 He joined AC Milan. On August 2015 He joined Lecce on loan. On January 2016 He joined Catania on loan. On Summer 2016 He joined Como on loan. On 7 July, 2017 He joined Atalanta. On 25 August 2017 He joined Spezia on loan. On 2023 He joined Monza back. On 20 June 2021 He did beat Wales 1-0 in UEFA Euro 2020 Matches. On 26 June 2021 He scored a goal and beat Austria in extra time 2-1 in UEFA Euro 2020 Matches. On 11 July 2021 He beat England with penalty shootout 1-1 and 3-2 in Penalty Shootout He won in UEFA Euro 2020. FIFA U-20 World Cup 3rd: 2017. UEFA European Championship: 2020.

Matteo Maria Zuppi (born 11 October 1955) is an Italian prelate of the Catholic Church who has been Archbishop of Bologna since 2015. He was an auxiliary bishop of Rome from 2012 to 2015. Pope Francis made him a cardinal in 2019. He has been president of the Episcopal Conference of Italy since May 2022. Zuppi is seen as a front-runner in the upcoming 2025 papal conclave to replace Pope Francis following his death.

Matthew Le Tissier (born 14 October 1968) is a former football player. He has played for Southampton and England national team. Southampton Player of the Season: 1989–90, 1993–94, 1994–95 Most assists in the Premier League: 1994–95 BBC Goal of the Month: October 1993, August 1994, December 1994 Premier League Player of the Month: December 1994, October 1996 PFA Team of the Year: 1994–95 Premier League

Matthew Avery Modine (born March 22, 1959) is an American actor, activist, director, producer, writer and cinematographer. His movie roles include Private Joker in Stanley Kubrick's Full Metal Jacket, the title character in Alan Parker's Birdy, high school wrestler Louden Swain in Vision Quest, football star turned spy Alec McCall in Funcky Monkey and the oversexed Sullivan Groff in Weeds. He appeared in Christopher Nolan's The Dark Knight Rises as Officer Peter Foley. He also played Dr. Martin Brenner in Netflix's Stranger Things. He unsuccessfully ran for National President of the SAG-AFTRA two times in 2019 and in 2021. Modine played Vannevar Bush in the 2023 Christopher Nolan movie Oppenheimer. Modine was born on March 22, 1959 in Loma Linda, California. He is the son of Dolores (née Warner), a bookkeeper, and Mark Alexander Modine, who managed a drive-in theater. He was educated at Brigham Young University. He was raised in Salt Lake City, Utah. Modine is married to Caridad Rivera since 1980 and have two children. His daughter, Ruby Modine, is an actress and dancer.

Matthew P. "Pat" Kennedy (28 January 1908 - 16 June 1957) was an American basketball referee. He was known for his emphatic, theatrical style. Kennedy is a member of the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame.
Matthew Glaetzer is a track cyclist from Australia. Glaetzer competed at the 2012 Summer Olympics, 2016 Summer Olympics, and the 2020 Summer Olympics. He was born on 24 August 1992.

Matthew James Kessel (born June 23, 2000) is an American professional ice hockey defenseman. He currently plays for the St. Louis Blues of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Kessel played one season with the Fargo Force, one season with the Chicago Steel, and one season with the Sioux Falls Stampede of the United States Hockey League (USHL), as well as, three years with the UMass Minutemen of Hockey East. He was drafted 150th overall by the St. Louis Blues in the 2020 NHL entry draft. On March 27, 2022, Kessel signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Blues. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Springfield Thunderbirds. On April 2, 2023, the Blues called him up and Kessel made his NHL debut in a 4–3 shootout loss against the Boston Bruins. On February 13, 2024, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Alexey Toropchenko goal in a 4–1 loss against the Toronto Maple Leafs. On March 13, 2024, Kessel signed a two-year contract to stay with the Blues.

Matthew Michael Knies (born October 17, 2002) is an American professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Columbus Blue Jackets of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Toronto Maple Leafs. Before playing in the NHL, Knies played three seasons with the Tri-City Storm of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and two years with the Minnesota Golden Gophers of the Big Ten Conference (B1G). He was named the Big Ten Player of the Year. He was also named to the All-Big Ten Freshman Team, All-Big Ten First Team, and All-Big Ten Second Team, as well as, a AHCA West First Team All-American. He was drafted 57th overall by the Toronto Maple Leafs of the 2021 NHL entry draft. On April 9, 2023, Knies signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Maple Leafs. On April 10, 2023, Knies made his NHL debut in a 2–1 overtime win against the Florida Panthers. The next day, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Ryan O'Reilly goal in a 4–3 win against the Tampa Bay Lightning. On October 21, Knies scored his first two NHL goals against Jonas Johansson in a 5–2 win against the Tampa Bay Lightning. On January 4, 2025, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 6–4 win against the Boston Bruins. On June 29, Knies signed a six-year, $46.5 million contract to stay with the Leafs. On September 28, 2026, the Leafs traded Knies along with a Steven Lorentz, Emil Andrae, 2027 conditional second-round draft pick to the Columbus Blue Jackets in exchange for Kirill Marchenko, Elvis Merzļikins, and Miles Wood.

Matthew Robertson (born March 9, 2001) is a Canadian professional ice hockey defenceman. He currently plays for the New York Rangers of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Robertson played parts of five seasons with the Edmonton Oil Kings of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He was drafted 210th overall by the New York Rangers of the 2012 NHL entry draft. On October 8, 2019, Robertson signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Rangers. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Hartford Wolf Pack. On July 15, 2024, Robertson signed a one-year contract to stay with the Rangers. On April 14, 2025, the Rangers called him up and Robertson made his NHL debut in a 5–3 win against the Florida Panthers. On June 20, Robertson signed a two-year contract to stay with the Rangers. On October 18, Robertson scored his first NHL goal against Sam Montembeault in a 4–3 win against the Montreal Canadiens.

Matthias Jaissle (born 5 April 1988) is a German football manager and former player who played as a defender. In 2021 he became the manager of FC Liefering and then manager of Red Bull Salzburg. He played for 1899 Hoffenheim when they were promoted to 2. Bundesliga and to Bundesliga the following season. On 3 April 2017 he became assistant of manager Alexander Zorniger of Brøndby IF starting from the summer 2017. He left Brøndby IF and became manager for FC Red Bull Salzburg's U18 academy team. In January 2021 he became new head coach of FC Liefering after Bo Svensson left the club. After the leaving of headcoach Jesse Marsch he became new head coach of FC Red Bull Salzburg for the new season. With the team he played in the UEFA Champions League where he is the youngest manager. For the first time FC Red Bull Salzburg plays in the knockout stage of the competition. He is the first manager of FC Red Bull Salzburg who is in office for three seasons. The German also started the 2023/24 season as Salzburg coach. After the opening match in the Austrian Cup, the club parted ways with Jaissle at the end of July 2023. He had entered into negotiations with al-Ahli shortly before the start of the league season. He then took over the Saudi team on the same day as his dismissal. On May 3, 2025, he led Al-Ahli to the final of the AFC Champions League Elite, They won 2-0 against the Japanese team Kawasaki Frontale. On the 5 August 2026 he joined Newcastle United as their new head coach following the departure of Eddie Howe. UEFA Champions League:Knock out stage: 2022

John Matthew Stafford (born February 7, 1988) is the starting American football quarterback for the Los Angeles Rams of the National Football League (NFL). He played college football in Georgia. He ranks in the top 20 for all-time in pass attempts, completions, passing yards, and passing touchdowns. Stafford is third in all-time passing yards per game. He was the fastest NFL player to reach 40,000 yards. Stafford was with the Detroit Lions from 2009 until 2020. In 2011, Stafford became the fourth NFL quarterback to throw for over 5,000 yards in a single season, while the Lions played in the playoffs for the first time since 1999.

Matthias Kaburek (9 February 1911 – 17 February 1976) was an Austrian football player. He played as a forward mainly for SK Rapid Wien. With the Austrian national football team he played in the 1934 FIFA World Cup. Kaburek started his career with the Vienna Cricket and Football-Club. In 1928 he went to SK Rapid Wien.Then he played for FC Metz (1936/37) and USB Longwy (1937/38) in the French league sides Metz, alongside compatriot and fellow World Cup player Franz Cisar. For Rapid Vienna, Kaburek played 152 games and scored 135 goals. He played his first match on 11 February 1934 in a 4-2 win versus Italy. As a player Kaburek was part of Austria national football team at the 1934 FIFA World Cup. He also played one match for Germany after the occupation of Austria by Nazi Germany in 1939. Matthew Wood (born February 6, 2005) is a Canadian professional ice hockey forward. He currently plays for the Nashville Predators of the National Hockey League (NHL). Before playing in the NHL, Wood played two seasons with the Victoria Grizzlies of the British Columbia Hockey League (BCHL), two years with the UConn Huskies of Hockey East, and one year with the Minnesota Golden Gophers of the Big Ten Conference (B1G). He had a successful time with his teams. With the Grizzlies, he won the Bruce Allison Memorial Trophy for bring rookie of the year and won the Brett Hull Trophy for being th BCHL's top scorer. He was also named to the All-Rookie Team and First All-Star Team. With the Huskies, he was named to the Hockey East All-Rookie Team. He was drafted 15th overall by the Nashville Predators in the 2023 NHL entry draft. On March 29, 2025, Wood signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Predators. On April 6, 2025, Wood made his NHL debut in a 2–1 loss against the Montreal Canadiens. On April 14, Wood recorded his first NHL point, assisting on a Michael Bunting goal in a 7–3 loss against the Utah Hockey Club. On October 30, 2025, Wood scored his first NHL goal against Daniel Vladař in a 4–1 loss against the Philadelphia Flyers.

Matthew Savoie (born January 1, 2004) is a Canadian professional ice hockey centre. He currently plays for the Edmonton Oilers of the National Hockey League (NHL). He has also played for the Buffalo Sabres. Before playing in the NHL, Savoie played parts of three seasons with the Winnipeg Ice of the Western Hockey League (WHL), four regular season games for the Sherwood Park Crusaders of the Alberta Junior Hockey League (AJHL), and one season with the Dubuque Fighting Saints of the United States Hockey League (USHL). He had a successful time with his teams. With the Fighting Saints, he was named to the All-Rookie Team. With the Ice, he was named to the East First All-Star Team. He was drafted 9th overall by the Buffalo Sabres in the 2022 NHL entry draft. On July 16, 2022, Savoie signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Sabres. He was sent down to play for their AHL-affiliate Rochester Americans. On November 10, 2023, the Sabres called him up and Savoie made his NHL debut in a 3–2 win against the Minnesota Wild. After the game he was sent back down to the AHL to play for the Americans. He also played for the Wenatchee Wild and Moose Jaw Warriors of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He won the Ed Chynoweth Cup with the Warriors in 2024. After a season with both, he was called back up to the Oilers. On July 5, 2024, the Sabres traded Savoie to the Edmonton Oilers in exchange for Ryan McLeod and Tyler Tullio. On February 22, 2025, he recorded his first NHL point after assisting on a Leon Draisaitl goal in a 6–3 loss against the Philadelphia Flyers. On October 30, Savoie scored his first NHL goal on the powerplay against Igor Shesterkin in a 4–3 overtime loss against the New York Rangers. On April 16, 2026, Savoie recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 6–1 win against the Vancouver Canucks.

Matthew Brendan Tkachuk (born December 11, 1997) is an American professional ice hockey winger. He currently plays for the Florida Panthers of the National Hockey League (NHL) and serves as an alternate captain. He has also played for the Calgary Flames. Tkachuk is a two-time Stanley Cup champion, winning back-to-back with the Panthers in 2024 and 2025. He is also a two-time All-Star, being named one in 2020 and 2023. He was the cover athlete for EA Sports' NHL 26 video game. Internationally, Tkachuk plays for the United States and won a gold medal in 2026. Before playing in the NHL, Tkachuk played two seasons with the U.S. National Development Team of the United States Hockey League (USHL) and one season with the London Knights of the Ontario Hockey League (OHL). He was drafted 6th overall by the Anaheim Ducks of the 2012 NHL entry draft. On July 7, 2016, Tkachuk signed a three-year entry-level contract to join the Flames. On October 12, 2016, Tkachuk made his NHL debut in a 7–4 loss against the Edmonton Oilers. On October 18, Tkachuk scored his first NHL goal against Robin Lehner in a 4–3 overtime win against the Buffalo Sabres. On March 20, 2017, the league suspended Tkachuk for two regular games after he intentionally elbowed Los Angeles Kings player Drew Doughty in the head during a game. On March 10, 2019, he recorded his first NHL hat-trick in a 6–3 win against the Vegas Golden Knights. On September 25, Tkachuk signed a three-year, $21 million contract to stay with the Flames. On July 22, 2022, the Flames traded Tkachuk along with a 2025 conditional fourth-round draft pick to the Florida Panthers in exchange for Jonathan Huberdeau, Cole Schwindt, MacKenzie Weegar, and a 2025 conditional first-round draft pick. He helped the Panthers during the playoffs. They defeated the Tampa Bay Lightning, Boston Bruins, and New York Rangers. They went on to defeat the Edmonton Oilers four games to three in the Final to win the first Stanley Cup in Panthers franchise history. Tkachuk and the Panthers made it back to the Stanley Cup Final the next year where they won their second Stanley Cup in a row. Tkachuk comes from a hockey family. His father Keith played 18 seasons in the NHL and his younger brother Brady is his teammate on the Panthers. Both Matthew and Brady were born in Scottsdale, Arizona when their father played for the Phoenix Coyotes.
